data.summary:
USER_CONTEXT: Implement full-stack Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System matching pinned OpenAPI + UI contracts. Clinical samples (home/clinic/collection point) must reach a lab before deadline; home samples require certified collector sealing before transport; then relay via couriers/centres/hubs.

TASK_TRACKING:
- Active: Implement full-stack system (backend Go + React frontend + schemas) matching OpenAPI + UI contracts
- Status: IN_PROGRESS — backend core + WS/server + frontend scaffolding in place; aligning remaining handlers/routes to pinned OpenAPI; frontend UI, setup scripts, and compile/fix cycle still pending

COMPLETED:
- Backend core files surveyed: users.go, audit.go, idempotency.go, network.go, requests.go, assignments.go, journeys.go, serviceability.go, work.go, ws.go, main.go, models.go, auth.go, httpx.go, db.go, util.go
- Schemas surveyed: schema/postgres.sql, schema/mongo.js
- Contracts inspected: openapi.contract.json (paths, request/response shapes extracted), ui.contract.json (27 UI scenarios)
- Frontend scaffolding present: package.json, vite.config.ts, src/api.ts, src/styles.css
- INSTRUCTION.md and workspace layout reviewed

PENDING:
- Align remaining backend handlers/routes with pinned OpenAPI paths and response shapes
- Finish frontend UI to match ui.contract.json scenarios
- Create app-setup scripts
- Compile/fix cycle and wire everything together

CURRENT_STATE:
- Backend: largely implemented (auth, users, network/locations, requests, assignments, journeys, serviceability, work, WS, audit, idempotency); some route/shape mismatches vs OpenAPI remain
- Frontend: Vite+React+maplibre scaffolding only (api.ts types/constants, styles); no full UI yet
- app-setup/: empty
- bin/: empty
- Contracts: OpenAPI + UI pinned; UI scenarios include login, role switch, role work view, sample status history, freshness, etc.

CODE_STATE:
- backend/: Go HTTP server (main.go openStore/ensureAdmin, gorilla/websocket, lib/pq + mongo-driver)
- frontend/: Vite React app, proxy /api /ready to :8080
- schema/postgres.sql: DROP+CREATE idempotent
- schema/mongo.js: audit_entries collections, drop+recreate

DEPS:
- Backend: github.com/google/uuid, github.com/lib/pq, go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver, github.com/gorilla/websocket, golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt
- Frontend: react 18, maplibre-gl, pmtiles, vite

VERSION_CONTROL_STATUS: Not a git-tracked feature branch focus; working in /workspace

     1	# Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System
     2	
     3	Clinical samples may start at a patient’s home, a clinic, or a collection point and must reach a suitable laboratory before their delivery deadline.
     4	
     5	Home samples must be collected and sealed by a certified collection professional before they can enter the transport network. Once sealed, a sample may pass through relay couriers, collection centres and hubs before reaching the laboratory.
     6	
     7	Dispatchers currently coordinate much of this work through calls, chat groups, and spreadsheets. This makes it difficult to track custody, use available capacity, assign work fairly, combine compatible samples, and recover when part of the network becomes unavailable.
     8	
     9	Build a web application that manages this entire process, from the initial serviceability check through laboratory receipt.
    10	
    11	## Users and responsibilities
    12	
    13	Use role-based access control for both actions and data: each user may perform actions and see data only as permitted by the role or roles they currently hold.
    14	
    15	For each of their roles, a user can see their current work and their past (completed) work, and can view a status timeline — the ordered history of status changes — for every item of work they are responsible for.
    16	
    17	A user may have more than one assigned role:
    18	
    19	- The user must explicitly select the role they are currently working under, and permissions and work views must use that selected role.
    20	- Switching role context must not add or remove any roles from the account.
    21	
    22	### Requester
    23	
    24	A requester should be able to:
    25	
    26	- Check whether a location and sample can be serviced before creating a request.
    27	- Create a home or clinic collection request.
    28	- Follow the sample’s current status, location, route and history.
    29	- See only requests that belong to them.
    30	
    31	The serviceability check must be a dry run. It must not create a request, sample, journey, assignment or capacity reservation.
    32	
    33	### Certified collection professional
    34	
    35	A certified collection professional should be able to:
    36	
    37	- View collection work for which they are qualified.
    38	- Accept or decline an offered collection assignment.
    39	- Record that a sample was collected and sealed.
    40	- Record their current location.
    41	- Hand off and confirm the transfer of the sealed sample to a relay courier or facility.
    42	
    43	### Relay courier
    44	
    45	A relay courier should be able to:
    46	
    47	- View delivery work assigned to them.
    48	- Accept or decline an offered transport assignment.
    49	- See only the details needed for their assigned leg.
    50	- Record location and progress updates.
    51	- Confirm pickup and handoff with the other party.
    52	
    53	### Node handler
    54	
    55	A node handler should be able to:
    56	
    57	- Accept or decline an offered node assignment.
    58	- Manage samples arriving at and leaving a collection centre or hub.
    59	- Register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system.
    60	- Confirm incoming and outgoing handoffs.
    61	- View and configure regular and cooled capacity at the node they are assigned to.
    62	
    63	### Laboratory intake operator
    64	
    65	A laboratory intake operator should be able to:
    66	
    67	- Accept or decline an offered laboratory assignment.
    68	- View expected samples and configure regular and cooled capacity at the laboratory they are assigned to.
    69	- Confirm that a sample was received.
    70	- Record an exception when a sample cannot be accepted normally.
    71	
    72	### Dispatcher
    73	
    74	A dispatcher should be able to:
    75	
    76	- Monitor samples, workers, collection nodes, laboratories, routes and exceptions.
    77	- See the current holder of each sample and whether its latest location is stale.
    78	- View the full journey, including collection and individual transport legs.
    79	- Change, split, merge, cancel or reroute unfinished work.
    80	- Replan unfinished work when a worker, node, route, laboratory or capacity pool becomes unavailable.
    81	- Search the complete audit history of a request or sample.
    82	
    83	Completed work and confirmed custody must not be rewritten during replanning.
    84	
    85	### Administrator
    86	
    87	An administrator may also do everything a dispatcher can do.
    88	
    89	In addition, only an administrator can:
    90	
    91	- Manage users, roles and professional certifications, including which node or laboratory a node handler or laboratory intake operator is assigned to.
    92	- Create and update collection nodes and laboratories.
    93	- Create and update sample types and their handling attributes.
    94	- Activate or deactivate a location, an individual function it provides, or a connection, without restarting the application.
    95	- Configure service coverage, travel times, handling times and laboratory capabilities.
    96	- Configure regular and cooled capacity for any node, laboratory, or transport connection.
    97	
    98	## Collection requests
    99	
   100	A collection request records where and when a sample can be collected and when it must reach the laboratory:
   101	
   102	- **Origin** — a patient’s home, a clinic, or a network node.
   103	- **Sample type** — see Sample types below.
   104	- **Collection window** — the earliest and latest time at which the sample may be collected. Collection must take place inside this window.
   105	- **Delivery deadline** — the time by which the sample must be received at the laboratory.
   106	
   107	The collection window and the delivery deadline are separate constraints: the window governs when pickup may happen, the deadline governs when laboratory receipt must happen. A plan is valid only when collection takes place within the collection window and the sample can still reach an accepting laboratory before its delivery deadline.
   108	
   109	## Pre-sealed samples
   110	
   111	A certified collection professional, relay courier, node handler, or laboratory intake operator may register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system — the person registering it must be the one who currently holds it.
   112	
   113	- Its origin must be a clinic or a network node — not a home.
   114	- The system should create only the transport legs needed from the point of registration onward.
   115	
   116	## Sample types
   117	
   118	Every sample has a type that determines its handling rules, and those rules apply for the whole journey, from collection through laboratory receipt. The system must have at least the following named types available by default: Amber, Indigo, Frost, Pulse. Each of the four requires a qualified collector — only a certified collection professional holding the matching qualification may collect it.
   119	
   120	- **Amber** — standard handling.
   121	- **Indigo** — must not share a container with an Amber sample.
   122	- **Frost** — requires cooled storage and transport throughout its entire journey.
   123	- **Pulse** — time-critical; it must not wait to be combined into a consolidation batch and must be routed without batching delay.
   124	
   125	These named rules are in addition to the generic handling attributes (container, temperature range, qualified-collector requirement, and incompatibilities).
   126	
   127	## Network locations
   128	
   129	The transport network is made up of locations. A single location — a node — may act as a collection point, a transfer point, a hub, a laboratory, or any combination of these (for example, a hub that also acts as a laboratory).
   130	
   131	- **Collection point** — where samples are collected from or enter the network. Serviceability is measured from active collection points.
   132	- **Transfer point / hub** — where a sample changes custody or moves between transport legs.
   133	- **Laboratory** — where a sample is received and its journey completes; a laboratory accepts specific sample types.
   134	
   135	A location may perform several of these functions at the same time.
   136	
   137	## Journey and assignment rules
   138	
   139	The system must support direct, multi-stop and batched journeys.
   140	
   141	A journey may contain several separately assigned transport legs. For example:
   142	
   143	1. Patient’s home to a local collection centre
   144	2. Local collection centre to a hub
   145	3. Hub to the laboratory
   146	
   147	Each movement between two locations is a separate assignment and may be handled by a different worker.
   148

   151	A requester should be able to perform this check independently of creating a request.
   152	
   153	The network's serviceability calculation must be published as one complete serviceability-calculation version at a time. While a new serviceability-calculation version is being computed, the system must keep serving the previous complete serviceability-calculation version, so that no request is checked against a partial or in-progress calculation.
   154	
   155	A batch is valid only when:
   156	
   157	- The assigned worker is eligible.
   158	- The samples are allowed to travel together.
   159	- Their container and temperature requirements are compatible.
   160	- Enough capacity is available.
   161	- Stops are in the correct order.
   162	- Every sample can still meet its deadline.
   163	
   164	Whenever a route or batch changes, validate every affected leg and capacity reservation against these same criteria. If that validation fails, reject the change and keep the current plan in place.
   165	
   166	## Capacity
   167	
   168	Collection nodes, laboratories and transport connections may have separate regular and cooled capacity, tracked as configured, reserved, and available units for both regular and cooled storage or transport.
   169	
   170	Capacity must be reserved when a journey is created and released when it is no longer required. The system must never overbook a capacity pool.
   171	
   172	## Chain of custody
   173	
   174	Every sealed sample must have exactly one current holder at all times.
   175	
   176	A handoff requires confirmation from both the sender and receiver. Until both sides confirm, the sender remains responsible for the sample. The receiver becomes the current holder only after the handoff is complete. Repeated or delayed handoff confirmations must not create duplicate transfers of custody. All custody changes must appear in the sample’s lifecycle and audit history. 
   177	
   178	At any point while holding custody of a sample, a certified collection professional, relay courier, node handler, or laboratory intake operator may record a handling checkpoint - the container type and temperature they currently observe. If the observed container or temperature falls outside the sample's required range, the sample must be marked as an exception.
   179	
   180	## Disruptions and replanning
   181	
   182	When part of a journey becomes unavailable:
   183	
   184	- Keep the current sample holder unchanged.
   185	- Preserve completed assignments, stops and handoffs.
   186	- Replan only unfinished work.
   187	- Allow only one active replacement plan.
   188	- Recheck worker eligibility, compatibility, capacity and deadlines.
   189	- Mark the sample as expired if no valid route can meet its deadline.
   190	
   191	Plan changes must use journey plan-version checks so that outdated updates cannot overwrite newer ones for that journey.
   192	
   193	## Tracking and audit
   194	
   195	Show routes, nodes, laboratories, and the current locations of certified collection professionals and relay couriers on a live map.
   196	
   197	For each sample, show:
   198	
   199	- Its current or last known location
   200	- Current custodian
   201	- Route progress
   202	- The time of its last update
   203	- Whether that location is stale
   204	
   205	Keep searchable audit logs covering sign-ins, permission checks, offers, collection, sealing, custody, routes, nodes, capacity, overrides, exceptions, and completion. Each audit record must capture the user, their role, the action taken, the affected item, the time, the outcome, and the relevant changes.
   206	
   207	## Technical requirements
   208	
   209	- Backend: Go
   210	- Frontend: React with TypeScript
   211	- Maps: MapLibre GL JS with the supplied local PMTiles map assets
   212	
   213	Document how to build, run, reset and test the complete application.
   214	
   215	The environment provides PostgreSQL, MongoDB, and Redis. Use the services that are appropriate for your design. You are not required to use every available datastore only because it is present. Application state that is expected to be durable must survive an ordinary application restart.
   216	
   217	## Application Setup and Handoff
   218	
   219	Create a `/workspace/app-setup` directory containing:
   220	
   221	- `manifest.json`

   223

   232	  "contractVersion": "1.0",
   233	  "commands": {
   234	    "build": ["bash", "app-setup/build.sh"],
   235	    "start": ["bash", "app-setup/start.sh"],
   236	    "reset": ["bash", "app-setup/reset.sh"]

   244	    "openapi": "app-setup/openapi.json"

   247	    "loginOperationId": "auth.login"

   249	  "datastoresUsed": ["postgresql", "mongodb"]
   250	}

   254	
   255	Command values are argument arrays and are executed from `/workspace`.

   257	- `build` must install or compile what the application needs and then exit.
   258	- `start` must run the application in the foreground and remain active until terminated. It must not leave detached application processes behind.

     1	# Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System
     2	
     3	Clinical samples may start at a patient’s home, a clinic, or a collection point and must reach a suitable laboratory before their delivery deadline.
     4	
     5	Home samples must be collected and sealed by a certified collection professional before they can enter the transport network. Once sealed, a sample may pass through relay couriers, collection centres and hubs before reaching the laboratory.
     6	
     7	Dispatchers currently coordinate much of this work through calls, chat groups, and spreadsheets. This makes it difficult to track custody, use available capacity, assign work fairly, combine compatible samples, and recover when part of the network becomes unavailable.
     8	
     9	Build a web application that manages this entire process, from the initial serviceability check through laboratory receipt.
    10	
    11	## Users and responsibilities
    12	
    13	Use role-based access control for both actions and data: each user may perform actions and see data only as permitted by the role or roles they currently hold.
    14	
    15	For each of their roles, a user can see their current work and their past (completed) work, and can view a status timeline — the ordered history of status changes — for every item of work they are responsible for.
    16	
    17	A user may have more than one assigned role:
    18	
    19	- The user must explicitly select the role they are currently working under, and permissions and work views must use that selected role.
    20	- Switching role context must not add or remove any roles from the account.
    21	
    22	### Requester
    23	
    24	A requester should be able to:
    25	
    26	- Check whether a location and sample can be serviced before creating a request.
    27	- Create a home or clinic collection request.
    28	- Follow the sample’s current status, location, route and history.
    29	- See only requests that belong to them.
    30	
    31	The serviceability check must be a dry run. It must not create a request, sample, journey, assignment or capacity reservation.
    32	
    33	### Certified collection professional
    34	
    35	A certified collection professional should be able to:
    36	
    37	- View collection work for which they are qualified.
    38	- Accept or decline an offered collection assignment.
    39	- Record that a sample was collected and sealed.
    40	- Record their current location.
    41	- Hand off and confirm the transfer of the sealed sample to a relay courier or facility.
    42	
    43	### Relay courier
    44	
    45	A relay courier should be able to:
    46	
    47	- View delivery work assigned to them.
    48	- Accept or decline an offered transport assignment.
    49	- See only the details needed for their assigned leg.
    50	- Record location and progress updates.
    51	- Confirm pickup and handoff with the other party.
    52	
    53	### Node handler
    54	
    55	A node handler should be able to:
    56	
    57	- Accept or decline an offered node assignment.
    58	- Manage samples arriving at and leaving a collection centre or hub.
    59	- Register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system.
    60	- Confirm incoming and outgoing handoffs.
    61	- View and configure regular and cooled capacity at the node they are assigned to.
    62	
    63	### Laboratory intake operator
    64	
    65	A laboratory intake operator should be able to:
    66	
    67	- Accept or decline an offered laboratory assignment.
    68	- View expected samples and configure regular and cooled capacity at the laboratory they are assigned to.
    69	- Confirm that a sample was received.
    70	- Record an exception when a sample cannot be accepted normally.
    71	
    72	### Dispatcher
    73	
    74	A dispatcher should be able to:
    75	
    76	- Monitor samples, workers, collection nodes, laboratories, routes and exceptions.
    77	- See the current holder of each sample and whether its latest location is stale.
    78	- View the full journey, including collection and individual transport legs.
    79	- Change, split, merge, cancel or reroute unfinished work.
    80	- Replan unfinished work when a worker, node, route, laboratory or capacity pool becomes unavailable.
    81	- Search the complete audit history of a request or sample.
    82	
    83	Completed work and confirmed custody must not be rewritten during replanning.
    84	
    85	### Administrator
    86	
    87	An administrator may also do everything a dispatcher can do.
    88	
    89	In addition, only an administrator can:
    90	
    91	- Manage users, roles and professional certifications, including which node or laboratory a node handler or laboratory intake operator is assigned to.
    92	- Create and update collection nodes and laboratories.
    93	- Create and update sample types and their handling attributes.
    94	- Activate or deactivate a location, an individual function it provides, or a connection, without restarting the application.
    95	- Configure service coverage, travel times, handling times and laboratory capabilities.
    96	- Configure regular and cooled capacity for any node, laboratory, or transport connection.
    97	
    98	## Collection requests
    99	
   100	A collection request records where and when a sample can be collected and when it must reach the laboratory:
   101	
   102	- **Origin** — a patient’s home, a clinic, or a network node.
   103	- **Sample type** — see Sample types below.
   104	- **Collection window** — the earliest and latest time at which the sample may be collected. Collection must take place inside this window.
   105	- **Delivery deadline** — the time by which the sample must be received at the laboratory.
   106	
   107	The collection window and the delivery deadline are separate constraints: the window governs when pickup may happen, the deadline governs when laboratory receipt must happen. A plan is valid only when collection takes place within the collection window and the sample can still reach an accepting laboratory before its delivery deadline.
   108	
   109	## Pre-sealed samples
   110	
   111	A certified collection professional, relay courier, node handler, or laboratory intake operator may register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system — the person registering it must be the one who currently holds it.
   112	
   113	- Its origin must be a clinic or a network node — not a home.
   114	- The system should create only the transport legs needed from the point of registration onward.
   115	
   116	## Sample types
   117	
   118	Every sample has a type that determines its handling rules, and those rules apply for the whole journey, from collection through laboratory receipt. The system must have at least the following named types available by default: Amber, Indigo, Frost, Pulse. Each of the four requires a qualified collector — only a certified collection professional holding the matching qualification may collect it.
   119	
   120	- **Amber** — standard handling.
   121	- **Indigo** — must not share a container with an Amber sample.
   122	- **Frost** — requires cooled storage and transport throughout its entire journey.
   123	- **Pulse** — time-critical; it must not wait to be combined into a consolidation batch and must be routed without batching delay.
   124	
   125	These named rules are in addition to the generic handling attributes (container, temperature range, qualified-collector requirement, and incompatibilities).
   126	
   127	## Network locations
   128	
   129	The transport network is made up of locations. A single location — a node — may act as a collection point, a transfer point, a hub, a laboratory, or any combination of these (for example, a hub that also acts as a laboratory).
   130	
   131	- **Collection point** — where samples are collected from or enter the network. Serviceability is measured from active collection points.
   132	- **Transfer point / hub** — where a sample changes custody or moves between transport legs.
   133	- **Laboratory** — where a sample is received and its journey completes; a laboratory accepts specific sample types.
   134	
   135	A location may perform several of these functions at the same time.
   136	
   137	## Journey and assignment rules
   138	
   139	The system must support direct, multi-stop and batched journeys.
   140	
   141	A journey may contain several separately assigned transport legs. For example:
   142	
   143	1. Patient’s home to a local collection centre
   144	2. Local collection centre to a hub
   145	3. Hub to the laboratory
   146	
   147	Each movement between two locations is a separate assignment and may be handled by a different worker.

   153	The network's serviceability calculation must be published as one complete serviceability-calculation version at a time. While a new serviceability-calculation version is being computed, the system must keep serving the previous complete serviceability-calculation version, so that no request is checked against a partial or in-progress calculation.
   154	
   155	A batch is valid only when:
   156	
   157	- The assigned worker is eligible.
   158	- The samples are allowed to travel together.
   159	- Their container and temperature requirements are compatible.
   160	- Enough capacity is available.
   161	- Stops are in the correct order.
   162	- Every sample can still meet its deadline.
   163	
   164	Whenever a route or batch changes, validate every affected leg and capacity reservation against these same criteria. If that validation fails, reject the change and keep the current plan in place.
   165	
   166	## Capacity
   167	
   168	Collection nodes, laboratories and transport connections may have separate regular and cooled capacity, tracked as configured, reserved, and available units for both regular and cooled storage or transport.
   169	
   170	Capacity must be reserved when a journey is created and released when it is no longer required. The system must never overbook a capacity pool.
   171	
   172	## Chain of custody
   173	
   174	Every sealed sample must have exactly one current holder at all times.
   175	
   176	A handoff requires confirmation from both the sender and receiver. Until both sides confirm, the sender remains responsible for the sample. The receiver becomes the current holder only after the handoff is complete. Repeated or delayed handoff confirmations must not create duplicate transfers of custody. All custody changes must appear in the sample’s lifecycle and audit history. 
   177	
   178	At any point while holding custody of a sample, a certified collection professional, relay courier, node handler, or laboratory intake operator may record a handling checkpoint - the container type and temperature they currently observe. If the observed container or temperature falls outside the sample's required range, the sample must be marked as an exception.
   179	
   180	## Disruptions and replanning
   181	
   182	When part of a journey becomes unavailable:
   183	
   184	- Keep the current sample holder unchanged.
   185	- Preserve completed assignments, stops and handoffs.
   186	- Replan only unfinished work.
   187	- Allow only one active replacement plan.
   188	- Recheck worker eligibility, compatibility, capacity and deadlines.
   189	- Mark the sample as expired if no valid route can meet its deadline.
   190	
   191	Plan changes must use journey plan-version checks so that outdated updates cannot overwrite newer ones for that journey.
   192	
   193	## Tracking and audit
   194	
   195	Show routes, nodes, laboratories, and the current locations of certified collection professionals and relay couriers on a live map.
   196	
   197	For each sample, show:
   198	
   199	- Its current or last known location

   203	- Whether that location is stale

TASK_TRACKING:
- Active: Implement full-stack system (backend Go + React frontend + schemas) matching OpenAPI + UI contracts
- Status: IN_PROGRESS — backend largely present; still aligning routes/response shapes to pinned contract; frontend scaffolding exists but incomplete; setup scripts missing

- Inspected workspace layout, INSTRUCTION.md, contracts, schemas
- Reviewed backend handlers: main.go, models.go, httpx.go, auth.go, work.go, requests.go, journeys.go, assignments.go, users.go, network.go, serviceability.go
- Reviewed frontend scaffolding: package.json, api.ts, index.html, vite.config.ts
- Extracted OpenAPI schemas (JourneyStop, JourneyLeg, RoleWork, AssignmentWorkItem, OperationsState, AuditEntry, LocationFunction, etc.) and all API paths

- Backend: Go store + handlers exist (roles: administrator, dispatcher, requester, collection_professional, delivery_partner, node_handler, lab); unused-import compile issues previously noted
- Frontend: Vite/React (maplibre-gl, pmtiles); SAMPLE_TYPES + ROLES in api.ts; proxies /api → :8080
- Schemas: schema/postgres.sql (idempotent DROP+CREATE), schema/mongo.js (audit_entries etc.)

     1	# Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System
     2	
     3	Clinical samples may start at a patient’s home, a clinic, or a collection point and must reach a suitable laboratory before their delivery deadline.
     4	
     5	Home samples must be collected and sealed by a certified collection professional before they can enter the transport network. Once sealed, a sample may pass through relay couriers, collection centres and hubs before reaching the laboratory.
     6	
     7	Dispatchers currently coordinate much of this work through calls, chat groups, and spreadsheets. This makes it difficult to track custody, use available capacity, assign work fairly, combine compatible samples, and recover when part of the network becomes unavailable.
     8	
     9	Build a web application that manages this entire process, from the initial serviceability check through laboratory receipt.
    10	
    11	## Users and responsibilities
    12	
    13	Use role-based access control for both actions and data: each user may perform actions and see data only as permitted by the role or roles they currently hold.
    14	
    15	For each of their roles, a user can see their current work and their past (completed) work, and can view a status timeline — the ordered history of status changes — for every item of work they are responsible for.
    16	
    17	A user may have more than one assigned role:
    18	
    19	- The user must explicitly select the role they are currently working under, and permissions and work views must use that selected role.
    20	- Switching role context must not add or remove any roles from the account.
    21	
    22	### Requester
    23	
    24	A requester should be able to:
    25	
    26	- Check whether a location and sample can be serviced before creating a request.
    27	- Create a home or clinic collection request.
    28	- Follow the sample’s current status, location, route and history.
    29	- See only requests that belong to them.
    30	
    31	The serviceability check must be a dry run. It must not create a request, sample, journey, assignment or capacity reservation.
    32	
    33	### Certified collection professional
    34	
    35	A certified collection professional should be able to:
    36	
    37	- View collection work for which they are qualified.
    38	- Accept or decline an offered collection assignment.
    39	- Record that a sample was collected and sealed.
    40	- Record their current location.
    41	- Hand off and confirm the transfer of the sealed sample to a relay courier or facility.
    42	
    43	### Relay courier
    44	
    45	A relay courier should be able to:
    46	
    47	- View delivery work assigned to them.
    48	- Accept or decline an offered transport assignment.
    49	- See only the details needed for their assigned leg.
    50	- Record location and progress updates.
    51	- Confirm pickup and handoff with the other party.
    52	
    53	### Node handler
    54	
    55	A node handler should be able to:
    56	
    57	- Accept or decline an offered node assignment.
    58	- Manage samples arriving at and leaving a collection centre or hub.
    59	- Register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system.
    60	- Confirm incoming and outgoing handoffs.
    61	- View and configure regular and cooled capacity at the node they are assigned to.
    62	
    63	### Laboratory intake operator
    64	
    65	A laboratory intake operator should be able to:
    66	
    67	- Accept or decline an offered laboratory assignment.
    68	- View expected samples and configure regular and cooled capacity at the laboratory they are assigned to.
    69	- Confirm that a sample was received.
    70	- Record an exception when a sample cannot be accepted normally.
    71	
    72	### Dispatcher
    73	
    74	A dispatcher should be able to:
    75	
    76	- Monitor samples, workers, collection nodes, laboratories, routes and exceptions.
    77	- See the current holder of each sample and whether its latest location is stale.
    78	- View the full journey, including collection and individual transport legs.
    79	- Change, split, merge, cancel or reroute unfinished work.
    80	- Replan unfinished work when a worker, node, route, laboratory or capacity pool becomes unavailable.
    81	- Search the complete audit history of a request or sample.
    82	
    83	Completed work and confirmed custody must not be rewritten during replanning.
    84

    86

--- INSTRUCTION ---
# Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System

Clinical samples may start at a patient’s home, a clinic, or a collection point and must reach a suitable laboratory before their delivery deadline.

Home samples must be collected and sealed by a certified collection professional before they can enter the transport network. Once sealed, a sample may pass through relay couriers, collection centres and hubs before reaching the laboratory.

Dispatchers currently coordinate much of this work through calls, chat groups, and spreadsheets. This makes it difficult to track custody, use available capacity, assign work fairly, combine compatible samples, and recover when part of the network becomes unavailable.

Build a web application that manages this entire process, from the initial serviceability check through laboratory receipt.

## Users and responsibilities

Use role-based access control for both actions and data: each user may perform actions and see data only as permitted by the role or roles they currently hold.

For each of their roles, a user can see their current work and their past (completed) work, and can view a status timeline — the ordered history of status changes — for every item of work they are responsible for.

A user may have more than one assigned role:

- The user must explicitly select the role they are currently working under, and permissions and work views must use that selected role.
- Switching role context must not add or remove any roles from the account.

### Requester

A requester should be able to:

- Check whether a location and sample can be serviced before creating a request.
- Create a home or clinic collection request.
- Follow the sample’s current status, location, route and history.
- See only requests that belong to them.

The serviceability check must be a dry run. It must not create a request, sample, journey, assignment or capacity reservation.

### Certified collection professional

A certified collection professional should be able to:

- View collection work for which they are qualified.
- Accept or decline an offered collection assignment.
- Record that a sample was collected and sealed.
- Record their current location.
- Hand off and confirm the transfer of the sealed sample to a relay courier or facility.

### Relay courier

A relay courier should be able to:

- View delivery work assigned to them.
- Accept or decline an offered transport assignment.
- See only the details needed for their assigned leg.
- Record location and progress updates.
- Confirm pickup and handoff with the other party.

### Node handler

A node handler should be able to:

- Accept or decline an offered node assignment.
- Manage samples arriving at and leaving a collection centre or hub.
- Register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system.
- Confirm incoming and outgoing handoffs.
- View and configure regular and cooled capacity at the node they are assigned to.

### Laboratory intake operator

A laboratory intake operator should be able to:

- Accept or decline an offered laboratory assignment.
- View expected samples and configure regular and cooled capacity at the laboratory they are assigned to.
- Confirm that a sample was received.
- Record an exception when a sample cannot be accepted normally.

### Dispatcher

A dispatcher should be able to:

- Monitor samples, workers, collection nodes, laboratories, routes and exceptions.
- See the current holder of each sample and whether its latest location is stale.
- View the full journey, including collection and individual transport legs.
- Change, split, merge, cancel or reroute unfinished work.
- Replan unfinished work when a worker, node, route, laboratory or capacity pool becomes unavailable.
- Search the complete audit history of a request or sample.

Completed work and confirmed custody must not be rewritten during replanning.

### Administrator

An administrator may also do everything a dispatcher can do.

In addition, only an administrator can:

- Manage users, roles and professional certifications, including which node or laboratory a node handler or laboratory intake operator is assigned to.
- Create and update collection nodes and laboratories.
- Create and update sample types and their handling attributes.
- Activate or deactivate a location, an individual function it provides, or a connection, without restarting the application.
- Configure service coverage, travel times, handling times and laboratory capabilities.
- Configure regular and cooled capacity for any node, laboratory, or transport connection.

## Collection requests

A collection request records where and when a sample can be collected and when it must reach the laboratory:

- **Origin** — a patient’s home, a clinic, or a network node.
- **Sample type** — see Sample types below.
- **Collection window** — the earliest and latest time at which the sample may be collected. Collection must take place inside this window.
- **Delivery deadline** — the time by which the sample must be received at the laboratory.

The collection window and the delivery deadline are separate constraints: the window governs when pickup may happen, the deadline governs when laboratory receipt must happen. A plan is valid only when collection takes place within the collection window and the sample can still reach an accepting laboratory before its delivery deadline.

## Pre-sealed samples

A certified collection professional, relay courier, node handler, or laboratory intake operator may register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system — the person registering it must be the one who currently holds it.

- Its origin must be a clinic or a network node — not a home.
- The system should create only the transport legs needed from the point of registration onward.

## Sample types

Every sample has a type that determines its handling rules, and those rules apply for the whole journey, from collection through laboratory receipt. The system must have at least the following named types available by default: Amber, Indigo, Frost, Pulse. Each of the four requires a qualified collector — only a certified collection professional holding the matching qualification may collect it.

- **Amber** — standard handling.
- **Indigo** — must not share a container with an Amber sample.
- **Frost** — requires cooled storage and transport throughout its entire journey.
- **Pulse** — time-critical; it must not wait to be combined into a consolidation batch and must be routed without batching delay.

These named rules are in addition to the generic handling attributes (container, temperature range, qualified-collector requirement, and incompatibilities).

## Network locations

The transport network is made up of locations. A single location — a node — may act as a collection point, a transfer point, a hub, a laboratory, or any combination of these (for example, a hub that also acts as a laboratory).

- **Collection point** — where samples are collected from or enter the network. Serviceability is measured from active collection points.
- **Transfer point / hub** — where a sample changes custody or moves between transport legs.
- **Laboratory** — where a sample is received and its journey completes; a laboratory accepts specific sample types.

A location may perform several of these functions at the same time.

## Journey and assignment rules

The system must support direct, multi-stop and batched journeys.

A journey may contain several separately assigned transport legs. For example:

1. Patient’s home to a local collection centre
2. Local collection centre to a hub
3. Hub to the laboratory

Each movement between two locations is a separate assignment and may be handled by a different worker.

Collection must happen before transport. Pickup must happen before delivery, and responsibility for the sample must be transferred through a confirmed handoff before the next person continues the journey.

Work should be assigned fairly among eligible and available workers:

- Consider each worker’s current workload and recent assignments.
- Offer an assignment to one worker at a time.
- A node or laboratory assignment may only be offered to a worker assigned to that specific node or laboratory
- A worker who declines an assignment may still receive suitable work later.
- An offer that receives no response within a reasonable time must be treated as declined and re-offered to the next eligible worker.
- If no qualified worker is ever available for an assignment that requires one, and none becomes available within a reasonable time, the sample must be flagged as an exception for that specific reason — distinguishable from a missed delivery deadline.
- Repeated declines may lower a worker’s priority for future offers for a limited time, but must never permanently exclude them from future work.
- An assignment cannot be accepted by someone other than the worker to whom it was offered.

## Serviceability

A request is serviceable only when:

- Its origin is within 5 km of an active collection node.
- The sample can reach an active laboratory that accepts its sample type.
- A valid route is available.
- Required regular or cooled capacity is available.
- All handling and container rules can be satisfied.
- The sample can reach the laboratory before its deadline.

Serviceability depends only on the structure of the network — active nodes, routes, laboratory capabilities, and capacity. The temporary availability of a particular staff member or vehicle at a given moment must not change the serviceable region.

A requester should be able to perform this check independently of creating a request.

The network's serviceability calculation must be published as one complete serviceability-calculation version at a time. While a new serviceability-calculation version is being computed, the system must keep serving the previous complete serviceability-calculation version, so that no request is checked against a partial or in-progress calculation.

A batch is valid only when:

- The assigned worker is eligible.
- The samples are allowed to travel together.
- Their container and temperature requirements are compatible.
- Enough capacity is available.
- Stops are in the correct order.
- Every sample can still meet its deadline.

Whenever a route or batch changes, validate every affected leg and capacity reservation against these same criteria. If that validation fails, reject the change and keep the current plan in place.

## Capacity

Collection nodes, laboratories and transport connections may have separate regular and cooled capacity, tracked as configured, reserved, and available units for both regular and cooled storage or transport.

Capacity must be reserved when a journey is created and released when it is no longer required. The system must never overbook a capacity pool.

## Chain of custody

Every sealed sample must have exactly one current holder at all times.

A handoff requires confirmation from both the sender and receiver. Until both sides confirm, the sender remains responsible for the sample. The receiver becomes the current holder only after the handoff is complete. Repeated or delayed handoff confirmations must not create duplicate transfers of custody. All custody changes must appear in the sample’s lifecycle and audit history.

--- README ---
# Public task inputs

The candidate receives the frozen API contract and UI contract in this directory. Evaluator-only
files remain outside `tasks/public/`.
--- INSTRUCTION ---
# Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System

Clinical samples may start at a patient’s home, a clinic, or a collection point and must reach a suitable laboratory before their delivery deadline.

Home samples must be collected and sealed by a certified collection professional before they can enter the transport network. Once sealed, a sample may pass through relay couriers, collection centres and hubs before reaching the laboratory.

Dispatchers currently coordinate much of this work through calls, chat groups, and spreadsheets. This makes it difficult to track custody, use available capacity, assign work fairly, combine compatible samples, and recover when part of the network becomes unavailable.

Build a web application that manages this entire process, from the initial serviceability check through laboratory receipt.

## Users and responsibilities

Use role-based access control for both actions and data: each user may perform actions and see data only as permitted by the role or roles they currently hold.

For each of their roles, a user can see their current work and their past (completed) work, and can view a status timeline — the ordered history of status changes — for every item of work they are responsible for.

A user may have more than one assigned role:

- The user must explicitly select the role they are currently working under, and permissions and work views must use that selected role.
- Switching role context must not add or remove any roles from the account.

### Requester

A requester should be able to:

- Check whether a location and sample can be serviced before creating a request.
- Create a home or clinic collection request.
- Follow the sample’s current status, location, route and history.
- See only requests that belong to them.

The serviceability check must be a dry run. It must not create a request, sample, journey, assignment or capacity reservation.

### Certified collection professional

A certified collection professional should be able to:

- View collection work for which they are qualified.
- Accept or decline an offered collection assignment.
- Record that a sample was collected and sealed.
- Record their current location.
- Hand off and confirm the transfer of the sealed sample to a relay courier or facility.

### Relay courier

A relay courier should be able to:

- View delivery work assigned to them.
- Accept or decline an offered transport assignment.
- See only the details needed for their assigned leg.
- Record location and progress updates.

     1	# Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System
     2	
     3	Clinical samples may start at a patient’s home, a clinic, or a collection point and must reach a suitable laboratory before their delivery deadline.
     4	
     5	Home samples must be collected and sealed by a certified collection professional before they can enter the transport network. Once sealed, a sample may pass through relay couriers, collection centres and hubs before reaching the laboratory.
     6	
     7	Dispatchers currently coordinate much of this work through calls, chat groups, and spreadsheets. This makes it difficult to track custody, use available capacity, assign work fairly, combine compatible samples, and recover when part of the network becomes unavailable.
     8	
     9	Build a web application that manages this entire process, from the initial serviceability check through laboratory receipt.
    10	
    11	## Users and responsibilities
    12	
    13	Use role-based access control for both actions and data: each user may perform actions and see data only as permitted by the role or roles they currently hold.
    14	
    15	For each of their roles, a user can see their current work and their past (completed) work, and can view a status timeline — the ordered history of status changes — for every item of work they are responsible for.
    16	
    17	A user may have more than one assigned role:
    18	
    19	- The user must explicitly select the role they are currently working under, and permissions and work views must use that selected role.
    20	- Switching role context must not add or remove any roles from the account.
    21	
    22	### Requester
    23	
    24	A requester should be able to:
    25	
    26	- Check whether a location and sample can be serviced before creating a request.
    27	- Create a home or clinic collection request.
    28	- Follow the sample’s current status, location, route and history.
    29	- See only requests that belong to them.
    30	
    31	The serviceability check must be a dry run. It must not create a request, sample, journey, assignment or capacity reservation.
    32	
    33	### Certified collection professional
    34	
    35	A certified collection professional should be able to:
    36	
    37	- View collection work for which they are qualified.
    38	- Accept or decline an offered collection assignment.
    39	- Record that a sample was collected and sealed.
    40	- Record their current location.
    41	- Hand off and confirm the transfer of the sealed sample to a relay courier or facility.
    42	
    43	### Relay courier
    44	
    45	A relay courier should be able to:
    46	
    47	- View delivery work assigned to them.
    48	- Accept or decline an offered transport assignment.
    49	- See only the details needed for their assigned leg.
    50	- Record location and progress updates.
    51	- Confirm pickup and handoff with the other party.
    52	
    53	### Node handler
    54	
    55	A node handler should be able to:
    56	
    57	- Accept or decline an offered node assignment.
    58	- Manage samples arriving at and leaving a collection centre or hub.
    59	- Register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system.
    60	- Confirm incoming and outgoing handoffs.
    61	- View and configure regular and cooled capacity at the node they are assigned to.
    62	
    63	### Laboratory intake operator
    64	
    65	A laboratory intake operator should be able to:
    66	
    67	- Accept or decline an offered laboratory assignment.
    68	- View expected samples and configure regular and cooled capacity at the laboratory they are assigned to.
    69	- Confirm that a sample was received.
    70	- Record an exception when a sample cannot be accepted normally.
    71	
    72	### Dispatcher
    73	
    74	A dispatcher should be able to:
    75	
    76	- Monitor samples, workers, collection nodes, laboratories, routes and exceptions.
    77	- See the current holder of each sample and whether its latest location is stale.
    78	- View the full journey, including collection and individual transport legs.
    79	- Change, split, merge, cancel or reroute unfinished work.

    '/ready',
]

for p in paths_of_interest:

    for method, body in op.items():
        print(f'\n### {method.upper()} {p}  op={body.get("operationId")}')

        if rb:
            schema = rb.get('content',{}).get('application/json',{}).get('schema',{})

            print('REQUEST props:', list(schema.get('properties',{}).keys()))
        params = body.get('parameters')
        if params:

        for code, resp in body.get('responses',{}).items():

                sch = resp.get('content',{}).get('application/json',{}).get('schema',{})
                data = sch.get('properties',{}).get('data', sch)

print('\n=== OperationsState workers ===')
print(json.dumps(spec['components']['schemas']['OperationsState']['properties']['workers'], indent=2)[:2000])

print(json.dumps(spec['components']['schemas']['OperationsState']['properties']['handoffs'], indent=2)[:1500])

print(json.dumps(spec['components']['schemas']['OperationsState']['properties']['exceptions'], indent=2)[:1500])

]

        print(f'\n### {method.upper()} {p}  op={body.get("operationId")}')

            schema = rb.get('content',{}).get('application/json',{}).get('schema',{})

            print('REQUEST props:', list(schema.get('properties',{}).keys()))
        params = body.get('parameters')
        if params:

        for code, resp in body.get('responses',{}).items():
            if code.startswith('2'):
                sch = resp.get('content',{}).get('application/json',{}).get('schema',{})
                data = sch.get('properties',{}).get('data', sch)
                print(f'RESP {code} required:', data.get('required') if isinstance(data, dict) else None)

                    if '$ref' in data:

TASK_TRACKING:
- Active: Implement full-stack system (backend Go + React frontend + schemas) matching OpenAPI + UI contracts
- Status: IN_PROGRESS — contract/schema survey largely done; next is systematic backend response alignment, frontend completion, and app-setup

- Backend mostly in place (Go handlers, PG+Mongo, auth, WS, idempotency)
- Extracted remaining OpenAPI shapes: Coordinate, UserAccount, SampleType, Connection, ServiceabilityCheck/Region, CollectionRequestResult, Handoff, DisruptionReport, JourneyPlan, UiBootstrap, Error, SampleLifecycle, OperationsState
- Inspected UI contract scenarios (login, role switch, sample views, freshness, custodian, etc.)
- Read backend handlers: requests.go, journeys.go, serviceability.go, work.go, network.go, assignments.go, auth.go, httpx.go, db.go, models.go, main.go, ws.go, idempotency.go, util.go
- Read schemas (postgres.sql journeys+, mongo.js audit_entries), frontend scaffold (api.ts SAMPLE_TYPES/ROLES, Vite+React+maplibre, styles)

PENDING:
- Fix remaining backend response contract mismatches (CollectionRequestResult, JourneyPlan, OperationsState, SampleLifecycle, serviceability labels)
- Finish React frontend to match UI contract scenarios
- Add app-setup
- Align any remaining schema/handler gaps

CURRENT_STATE:
- Workspace: /workspace/{backend, frontend, contracts, schema, app-setup, bin}
- Backend: Store{PG, Mongo, Audit}; roles admin/dispatcher/requester/collection_professional/delivery_partner/node_handler/lab
- Key response shapes seen: CollectionRequestResult {requestId, sampleId, serviceability, serviceabilityReason, serviceabilityVersion, journeyId?, targetLaboratory…}; JourneyPlan {journeyId, planVersion, routeMode, status, estimatedDeliveryAt, totalCostUnits, capacityUsed…}

- contracts/{openapi.contract.json, ui.contract.json}

     1	# Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System
     2	
     3	Clinical samples may start at a patient’s home, a clinic, or a collection point and must reach a suitable laboratory before their delivery deadline.
     4	
     5	Home samples must be collected and sealed by a certified collection professional before they can enter the transport network. Once sealed, a sample may pass through relay couriers, collection centres and hubs before reaching the laboratory.
     6	
     7	Dispatchers currently coordinate much of this work through calls, chat groups, and spreadsheets. This makes it difficult to track custody, use available capacity, assign work fairly, combine compatible samples, and recover when part of the network becomes unavailable.
     8	
     9	Build a web application that manages this entire process, from the initial serviceability check through laboratory receipt.
    10	
    11	## Users and responsibilities
    12	
    13	Use role-based access control for both actions and data: each user may perform actions and see data only as permitted by the role or roles they currently hold.
    14	
    15	For each of their roles, a user can see their current work and their past (completed) work, and can view a status timeline — the ordered history of status changes — for every item of work they are responsible for.
    16	
    17	A user may have more than one assigned role:
    18	
    19	- The user must explicitly select the role they are currently working under, and permissions and work views must use that selected role.
    20	- Switching role context must not add or remove any roles from the account.
    21	
    22	### Requester
    23	
    24	A requester should be able to:
    25	
    26	- Check whether a location and sample can be serviced before creating a request.
    27	- Create a home or clinic collection request.
    28	- Follow the sample’s current status, location, route and history.
    29	- See only requests that belong to them.
    30	
    31	The serviceability check must be a dry run. It must not create a request, sample, journey, assignment or capacity reservation.
    32	
    33	### Certified collection professional
    34	
    35	A certified collection professional should be able to:
    36	
    37	- View collection work for which they are qualified.
    38	- Accept or decline an offered collection assignment.
    39	- Record that a sample was collected and sealed.
    40	- Record their current location.
    41	- Hand off and confirm the transfer of the sealed sample to a relay courier or facility.
    42	
    43	### Relay courier
    44	
    45	A relay courier should be able to:
    46	
    47	- View delivery work assigned to them.
    48	- Accept or decline an offered transport assignment.
    49	- See only the details needed for their assigned leg.
    50	- Record location and progress updates.
    51	- Confirm pickup and handoff with the other party.
    52	
    53	### Node handler
    54	
    55	A node handler should be able to:
    56	
    57	- Accept or decline an offered node assignment.
    58	- Manage samples arriving at and leaving a collection centre or hub.
    59	- Register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system.
    60	- Confirm incoming and outgoing handoffs.
    61	- View and configure regular and cooled capacity at the node they are assigned to.
    62	
    63	### Laboratory intake operator
    64	
    65	A laboratory intake operator should be able to:
    66	
    67	- Accept or decline an offered laboratory assignment.
    68	- View expected samples and configure regular and cooled capacity at the laboratory they are assigned to.
    69	- Confirm that a sample was received.
    70	- Record an exception when a sample cannot be accepted normally.
    71	
    72	### Dispatcher
    73	
    74	A dispatcher should be able to:
    75	
    76	- Monitor samples, workers, collection nodes, laboratories, routes and exceptions.
    77	- See the current holder of each sample and whether its latest location is stale.
    78	- View the full journey, including collection and individual transport legs.
    79	- Change, split, merge, cancel or reroute unfinished work.
    80	- Replan unfinished work when a worker, node, route, laboratory or capacity pool becomes unavailable.
    81	- Search the complete audit history of a request or sample.
    82	
    83	Completed work and confirmed custody must not be rewritten during replanning.
    84	
    85	### Administrator
    86	
    87	An administrator may also do everything a dispatcher can do.
    88	
    89	In addition, only an administrator can:
    90	
    91	- Manage users, roles and professional certifications, including which node or laboratory a node handler or laboratory intake operator is assigned to.
    92	- Create and update collection nodes and laboratories.
    93	- Create and update sample types and their handling attributes.
    94	- Activate or deactivate a location, an individual function it provides, or a connection, without restarting the application.
    95	- Configure service coverage, travel times, handling times and laboratory capabilities.
    96	- Configure regular and cooled capacity for any node, laboratory, or transport connection.
    97	
    98	## Collection requests
    99	
   100	A collection request records where and when a sample can be collected and when it must reach the laboratory:
   101	
   102	- **Origin** — a patient’s home, a clinic, or a network node.
   103	- **Sample type** — see Sample types below.
   104	- **Collection window** — the earliest and latest time at which the sample may be collected. Collection must take place inside this window.
   105	- **Delivery deadline** — the time by which the sample must be received at the laboratory.
   106	
   107	The collection window and the delivery deadline are separate constraints: the window governs when pickup may happen, the deadline governs when laboratory receipt must happen. A plan is valid only when collection takes place within the collection window and the sample can still reach an accepting laboratory before its delivery deadline.
   108	
   109	## Pre-sealed samples
   110	
   111	A certified collection professional, relay courier, node handler, or laboratory intake operator may register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system — the person registering it must be the one who currently holds it.
   112	
   113	- Its origin must be a clinic or a network node — not a home.
   114	- The system should create only the transport legs needed from the point of registration onward.
   115	
   116	## Sample types
   117	
   118	Every sample has a type that determines its handling rules, and those rules apply for the whole journey, from collection through laboratory receipt. The system must have at least the following named types available by default: Amber, Indigo, Frost, Pulse. Each of the four requires a qualified collector — only a certified collection professional holding the matching qualification may collect it.
   119	
   120	- **Amber** — standard handling.
   121	- **Indigo** — must not share a container with an Amber sample.
   122	- **Frost** — requires cooled storage and transport throughout its entire journey.
   123	- **Pulse** — time-critical; it must not wait to be combined into a consolidation batch and must be routed without batching delay.
   124	
   125	These named rules are in addition to the generic handling attributes (container, temperature range, qualified-collector requirement, and incompatibilities).
   126	
   127	## Network locations
   128	
   129	The transport network is made up of locations. A single location — a node — may act as a collection point, a transfer point, a hub, a laboratory, or any combination of these (for example, a hub that also acts as a laboratory).
   130	
   131	- **Collection point** — where samples are collected from or enter the network. Serviceability is measured from active collection points.
   132	- **Transfer point / hub** — where a sample changes custody or moves between transport legs.
   133	- **Laboratory** — where a sample is received and its journey completes; a laboratory accepts specific sample types.
   134	
   135	A location may perform several of these functions at the same time.
   136	
   137	## Journey and assignment rules
   138	
   139	The system must support direct, multi-stop and batched journeys.
   140	
   141	A journey may contain several separately assigned transport legs. For example:
   142	
   143	1. Patient’s home to a local collection centre
   144	2. Local collection centre to a hub
   145	3. Hub to the laboratory
   146	
   147	Each movement between two locations is a separate assignment and may be handled by a different worker.
   148	
   149	Collection must happen before transport. Pickup must happen before delivery, and responsibility for the sample must be transferred through a confirmed handoff before the next person continues the journey.
   150	
   151	Work should be assigned fairly among eligible and available workers:
   152	
   153	- Consider each worker’s current workload and recent assignments.
   154	- Offer an assignment to one worker at a time.
   155	- A node or laboratory assignment may only be offered to a worker assigned to that specific node or laboratory
   156	- A worker who declines an assignment may still receive suitable work later.
   157	- An offer that receives no response within a reasonable time must be treated as declined and re-offered to the next eligible worker.
   158	- If no qualified worker is ever available for an assignment that requires one, and none becomes available within a reasonable time, the sample must be flagged as an exception for that specific reason — distinguishable from a missed delivery deadline.
   159	- Repeated declines may lower a worker’s priority for future offers for a limited time, but must never permanently exclude them from future work.
   160	- An assignment cannot be accepted by someone other than the worker to whom it was offered.
   161	
   162	## Serviceability
   163	
   164	A request is serviceable only when:
   165	
   166	- Its origin is within 5 km of an active collection node.
   167	- The sample can reach an active laboratory that accepts its sample type.
   168	- A valid route is available.
   169	- Required regular or cooled capacity is available.
   170	- All handling and container rules can be satisfied.
   171	- The sample can reach the laboratory before its deadline.
   172	
   173	Serviceability depends only on the structure of the network — active nodes, routes, laboratory capabilities, and capacity. The temporary availability of a particular staff member or vehicle at a given moment must not change the serviceable region.
   174	
   175	A requester should be able to perform this check independently of creating a request.
   176	
   177	The network's serviceability calculation must be published as one complete serviceability-calculation version at a time. While a new serviceability-calculation version is being computed, the system must keep serving the previous complete serviceability-calculation version, so that no request is checked against a partial or in-progress calculation.
   178	
   179	A batch is valid only when:
   180	
   181	- The assigned worker is eligible.
   182	- The samples are allowed to travel together.
   183	- Their container and temperature requirements are compatible.
   184	- Enough capacity is available.
   185	- Stops are in the correct order.
   186	- Every sample can still meet its deadline.
   187	
   188	Whenever a route or batch changes, validate every affected leg and capacity reservation against these same criteria. If that validation fails, reject the change and keep the current plan in place.
   189	
   190	## Capacity
   191	
   192	Collection nodes, laboratories and transport connections may have separate regular and cooled capacity, tracked as configured, reserved, and available units for both regular and cooled storage or transport.
   193	
   194	Capacity must be reserved when a journey is created and released when it is no longer required. The system must never overbook a capacity pool.
   195	
   196	## Chain of custody
   197	
   198	Every sealed sample must have exactly one current holder at all times.
   199	
   200	A handoff requires confirmation from both the sender and receiver. Until both sides confirm, the sender remains responsible for the sample. The receiver becomes the current holder only after the handoff is complete. Repeated or delayed handoff confirmations must not create duplicate transfers of custody. All custody changes must appear in the sample’s lifecycle and audit history.

TASK_TRACKING:
- Active: Implement full-stack system (backend Go + React frontend + schemas) matching OpenAPI + UI contracts
- Status: IN_PROGRESS — contract/schema survey largely done; next is systematically aligning remaining backend response shapes, then finishing frontend + app-setup

PENDING:

- Complete app-setup
- Verify end-to-end against OpenAPI + UI contracts

CURRENT_STATE:

     1	# Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System
     2	
     3	Clinical samples may start at a patient’s home, a clinic, or a collection point and must reach a suitable laboratory before their delivery deadline.
     4	
     5	Home samples must be collected and sealed by a certified collection professional before they can enter the transport network. Once sealed, a sample may pass through relay couriers, collection centres and hubs before reaching the laboratory.
     6	
     7	Dispatchers currently coordinate much of this work through calls, chat groups, and spreadsheets. This makes it difficult to track custody, use available capacity, assign work fairly, combine compatible samples, and recover when part of the network becomes unavailable.
     8	
     9	Build a web application that manages this entire process, from the initial serviceability check through laboratory receipt.
    10	
    11	## Users and responsibilities
    12	
    13	Use role-based access control for both actions and data: each user may perform actions and see data only as permitted by the role or roles they currently hold.
    14	
    15	For each of their roles, a user can see their current work and their past (completed) work, and can view a status timeline — the ordered history of status changes — for every item of work they are responsible for.
    16	
    17	A user may have more than one assigned role:
    18	
    19	- The user must explicitly select the role they are currently working under, and permissions and work views must use that selected role.
    20	- Switching role context must not add or remove any roles from the account.
    21

    23	
    24	A requester should be able to:
    25

    28	- Follow the sample’s current status, location, route and history.
    29	- See only requests that belong to them.
    30	
    31	The serviceability check must be a dry run. It must not create a request, sample, journey, assignment or capacity reservation.
    32

    34	
    35	A certified collection professional should be able to:
    36	
    37	- View collection work for which they are qualified.
    38	- Accept or decline an offered collection assignment.
    39	- Record that a sample was collected and sealed.
    40	- Record their current location.
    41	- Hand off and confirm the transfer of the sealed sample to a relay courier or facility.
    42	
    43	### Relay courier
    44	
    45	A relay courier should be able to:
    46	
    47	- View delivery work assigned to them.
    48	- Accept or decline an offered transport assignment.
    49	- See only the details needed for their assigned leg.
    50	- Record location and progress updates.
    51	- Confirm pickup and handoff with the other party.
    52	
    53	### Node handler
    54	
    55	A node handler should be able to:
    56	
    57	- Accept or decline an offered node assignment.
    58	- Manage samples arriving at and leaving a collection centre or hub.
    59	- Register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system.
    60	- Confirm incoming and outgoing handoffs.
    61	- View and configure regular and cooled capacity at the node they are assigned to.
    62	
    63	### Laboratory intake operator
    64	
    65	A laboratory intake operator should be able to:
    66	
    67	- Accept or decline an offered laboratory assignment.

    71

TASK_TRACKING:
- Active: Implement full-stack system (backend Go + React frontend + schemas) matching OpenAPI + UI contracts
- Status: IN_PROGRESS — contract/schema/handler survey in progress; mapping mismatches then aligning backend responses, finishing frontend, completing app-setup

- Inspected backend handlers: network.go, journeys.go, serviceability.go, db.go, users.go, ws.go, util.go, work.go, requests.go, main.go, httpx.go
- Inspected schemas: postgres.sql (journeys table + indexes), mongo.js (audit collections)
- Inspected contracts: openapi.contract.json, ui.contract.json (UI scenarios listed)
- Inspected frontend scaffold: package.json (React+Vite+maplibre), vite.config.ts (proxies /api to :8080), index.html, api.ts (SAMPLE_TYPES, ROLES), styles.css
- Inspected INSTRUCTION.md (full product spec) and README.md
- Workspace layout confirmed: app-setup/, backend/, bin/, contracts/, frontend/

PENDING:
- Finish remaining handler/frontend inspection
- Align backend responses to OpenAPI contract
- Complete React frontend for all UI contract scenarios
- Complete app-setup

CURRENT_STATE:
- Backend: Go HTTP server with Store{PG, Mongo, Audit}; handlers for auth, network, journeys, serviceability, work, requests, websocket
- Frontend: Vite+React scaffold exists but UI not fully built (no main.tsx/App visible yet in survey)
- UI scenarios: login_rejects_invalid_credentials, role_switch_control_lists_and_applies_role, role_work_view_shows_current_and_past, sample_view_shows_ordered_status_history, sample_freshnes...
- Contract mismatches identified; agent planning systematic alignment

CODE_STATE:
- backend/: main.go, httpx.go, network.go, journeys.go, serviceability.go, db.go, users.go, ws.go, util.go, work.go, requests.go
- schema/postgres.sql: journeys table (journey_id UUID PK, parent_journey_id, plan_version, route_mode, status)
- schema/mongo.js: audit_entries collection
- frontend/src/: api.ts, styles.css, vite-env.d.ts (main.tsx referenced by index.html, not yet inspected)
- contracts/: openapi.contract.json, ui.contract.json

- Align backend response shapes to pinned OpenAPI contract

- Frontend scaffold only: index.html, api.ts (SAMPLE_TYPES + ROLES), styles.css, vite.config.ts; no main.tsx/App components visible
- frontend/public/ empty; app-setup/ empty

DEPS: Go (bcrypt, uuid, mongo-driver, database/sql); React + Vite frontend

     1	# Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System
     2	
     3	Clinical samples may start at a patient’s home, a clinic, or a collection point and must reach a suitable laboratory before their delivery deadline.
     4	
     5	Home samples must be collected and sealed by a certified collection professional before they can enter the transport network. Once sealed, a sample may pass through relay couriers, collection centres and hubs before reaching the laboratory.
     6	
     7	Dispatchers currently coordinate much of this work through calls, chat groups, and spreadsheets. This makes it difficult to track custody, use available capacity, assign work fairly, combine compatible samples, and recover when part of the network becomes unavailable.
     8	
     9	Build a web application that manages this entire process, from the initial serviceability check through laboratory receipt.
    10	
    11	## Users and responsibilities
    12	
    13	Use role-based access control for both actions and data: each user may perform actions and see data only as permitted by the role or roles they currently hold.
    14	
    15	For each of their roles, a user can see their current work and their past (completed) work, and can view a status timeline — the ordered history of status changes — for every item of work they are responsible for.
    16	
    17	A user may have more than one assigned role:
    18	
    19	- The user must explicitly select the role they are currently working under, and permissions and work views must use that selected role.
    20	- Switching role context must not add or remove any roles from the account.
    21	
    22	### Requester
    23	
    24	A requester should be able to:
    25	
    26	- Check whether a location and sample can be serviced before creating a request.
    27	- Create a home or clinic collection request.
    28	- Follow the sample’s current status, location, route and history.
    29	- See only requests that belong to them.
    30	
    31	The serviceability check must be a dry run. It must not create a request, sample, journey, assignment or capacity reservation.
    32	
    33	### Certified collection professional
    34	
    35	A certified collection professional should be able to:
    36	
    37	- View collection work for which they are qualified.
    38	- Accept or decline an offered collection assignment.
    39	- Record that a sample was collected and sealed.
    40	- Record their current location.
    41	- Hand off and confirm the transfer of the sealed sample to a relay courier or facility.
    42	
    43	### Relay courier
    44	
    45	A relay courier should be able to:
    46	
    47	- View delivery work assigned to them.
    48	- Accept or decline an offered transport assignment.
    49	- See only the details needed for their assigned leg.
    50	- Record location and progress updates.
    51	- Confirm pickup and handoff with the other party.
    52	
    53	### Node handler
    54	
    55	A node handler should be able to:
    56	
    57	- Accept or decline an offered node assignment.
    58	- Manage samples arriving at and leaving a collection centre or hub.
    59	- Register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system.
    60	- Confirm incoming and outgoing handoffs.
    61	- View and configure regular and cooled capacity at the node they are assigned to.
    62	
    63	### Laboratory intake operator
    64	
    65	A laboratory intake operator should be able to:
    66	
    67	- Accept or decline an offered laboratory assignment.
    68	- View expected samples and configure regular and cooled capacity at the laboratory they are assigned to.
    69	- Confirm that a sample was received.
    70	- Record an exception when a sample cannot be accepted normally.
    71	
    72	### Dispatcher
    73	
    74	A dispatcher should be able to:
    75	
    76	- Monitor samples, workers, collection nodes, laboratories, routes and exceptions.
    77	- See the current holder of each sample and whether its latest location is stale.
    78	- View the full journey, including collection and individual transport legs.
    79	- Change, split, merge, cancel or reroute unfinished work.
    80	- Replan unfinished work when a worker, node, route, laboratory or capacity pool becomes unavailable.
    81	- Search the complete audit history of a request or sample.
    82	
    83	Completed work and confirmed custody must not be rewritten during replanning.
    84	
    85	### Administrator
    86	
    87	An administrator may also do everything a dispatcher can do.
    88	
    89	In addition, only an administrator can:
    90	
    91	- Manage users, roles and professional certifications, including which node or laboratory a node handler or laboratory intake operator is assigned to.
    92	- Create and update collection nodes and laboratories.
    93	- Create and update sample types and their handling attributes.
    94	- Activate or deactivate a location, an individual function it provides, or a connection, without restarting the application.
    95	- Configure service coverage, travel times, handling times and laboratory capabilities.
    96	- Configure regular and cooled capacity for any node, laboratory, or transport connection.
