     1	# Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System
     2	
     3	Clinical samples may start at a patient’s home, a clinic, or a collection point and must reach a suitable laboratory before their delivery deadline.
     4	
     5	Home samples must be collected and sealed by a certified collection professional before they can enter the transport network. Once sealed, a sample may pass through relay couriers, collection centres and hubs before reaching the laboratory.
     6	
     7	Dispatchers currently coordinate much of this work through calls, chat groups, and spreadsheets. This makes it difficult to track custody, use available capacity, assign work fairly, combine compatible samples, and recover when part of the network becomes unavailable.
     8	
     9	Build a web application that manages this entire process, from the initial serviceability check through laboratory receipt.
    10	
    11	## Users and responsibilities
    12	
    13	Use role-based access control for both actions and data: each user may perform actions and see data only as permitted by the role or roles they currently hold.
    14	
    15	For each of their roles, a user can see their current work and their past (completed) work, and can view a status timeline — the ordered history of status changes — for every item of work they are responsible for.
    16	
    17	A user may have more than one assigned role:
    18	
    19	- The user must explicitly select the role they are currently working under, and permissions and work views must use that selected role.
    20	- Switching role context must not add or remove any roles from the account.
    21	
    22	### Requester
    23	
    24	A requester should be able to:
    25	
    26	- Check whether a location and sample can be serviced before creating a request.
    27	- Create a home or clinic collection request.
    28	- Follow the sample’s current status, location, route and history.
    29	- See only requests that belong to them.
    30	
    31	The serviceability check must be a dry run. It must not create a request, sample, journey, assignment or capacity reservation.
    32	
    33	### Certified collection professional
    34	
    35	A certified collection professional should be able to:
    36	
    37	- View collection work for which they are qualified.
    38	- Accept or decline an offered collection assignment.
    39	- Record that a sample was collected and sealed.
    40	- Record their current location.
    41	- Hand off and confirm the transfer of the sealed sample to a relay courier or facility.
    42	
    43	### Relay courier
    44	
    45	A relay courier should be able to:
    46	
    47	- View delivery work assigned to them.
    48	- Accept or decline an offered transport assignment.
    49	- See only the details needed for their assigned leg.
    50	- Record location and progress updates.
    51	- Confirm pickup and handoff with the other party.
    52	
    53	### Node handler
    54	
    55	A node handler should be able to:
    56	
    57	- Accept or decline an offered node assignment.
    58	- Manage samples arriving at and leaving a collection centre or hub.
    59	- Register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system.
    60	- Confirm incoming and outgoing handoffs.
    61	- View and configure regular and cooled capacity at the node they are assigned to.
    62	
    63	### Laboratory intake operator
    64	
    65	A laboratory intake operator should be able to:
    66	
    67	- Accept or decline an offered laboratory assignment.
    68	- View expected samples and configure regular and cooled capacity at the laboratory they are assigned to.
    69	- Confirm that a sample was received.
    70	- Record an exception when a sample cannot be accepted normally.
    71	
    72	### Dispatcher
    73	
    74	A dispatcher should be able to:
    75	
    76	- Monitor samples, workers, collection nodes, laboratories, routes and exceptions.
    77	- See the current holder of each sample and whether its latest location is stale.
    78	- View the full journey, including collection and individual transport legs.
    79	- Change, split, merge, cancel or reroute unfinished work.
    80	- Replan unfinished work when a worker, node, route, laboratory or capacity pool becomes unavailable.
    81	- Search the complete audit history of a request or sample.
    82	
    83	Completed work and confirmed custody must not be rewritten during replanning.
    84	
    85	### Administrator
    86	
    87	An administrator may also do everything a dispatcher can do.
    88	
    89	In addition, only an administrator can:
    90	
    91	- Manage users, roles and professional certifications, including which node or laboratory a node handler or laboratory intake operator is assigned to.
    92	- Create and update collection nodes and laboratories.
    93	- Create and update sample types and their handling attributes.
    94	- Activate or deactivate a location, an individual function it provides, or a connection, without restarting the application.
    95	- Configure service coverage, travel times, handling times and laboratory capabilities.
    96	- Configure regular and cooled capacity for any node, laboratory, or transport connection.
    97	
    98	## Collection requests
    99	
   100	A collection request records where and when a sample can be collected and when it must reach the laboratory:
   101	
   102	- **Origin** — a patient’s home, a clinic, or a network node.
   103	- **Sample type** — see Sample types below.
   104	- **Collection window** — the earliest and latest time at which the sample may be collected. Collection must take place inside this window.
   105	- **Delivery deadline** — the time by which the sample must be received at the laboratory.
   106	
   107	The collection window and the delivery deadline are separate constraints: the window governs when pickup may happen, the deadline governs when laboratory receipt must happen. A plan is valid only when collection takes place within the collection window and the sample can still reach an accepting laboratory before its delivery deadline.
   108	
   109	## Pre-sealed samples
   110	
   111	A certified collection professional, relay courier, node handler, or laboratory intake operator may register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system — the person registering it must be the one who currently holds it.
   112	
   113	- Its origin must be a clinic or a network node — not a home.
   114	- The system should create only the transport legs needed from the point of registration onward.
   115	
   116	## Sample types
   117	
   118	Every sample has a type that determines its handling rules, and those rules apply for the whole journey, from collection through laboratory receipt. The system must have at least the following named types available by default: Amber, Indigo, Frost, Pulse. Each of the four requires a qualified collector — only a certified collection professional holding the matching qualification may collect it.
   119	
   120	- **Amber** — standard handling.
   121	- **Indigo** — must not share a container with an Amber sample.
   122	- **Frost** — requires cooled storage and transport throughout its entire journey.
   123	- **Pulse** — time-critical; it must not wait to be combined into a consolidation batch and must be routed without batching delay.
   124	
   125	These named rules are in addition to the generic handling attributes (container, temperature range, qualified-collector requirement, and incompatibilities).
   126	
   127	## Network locations
   128	
   129	The transport network is made up of locations. A single location — a node — may act as a collection point, a transfer point, a hub, a laboratory, or any combination of these (for example, a hub that also acts as a laboratory).
   130	
   131	- **Collection point** — where samples are collected from or enter the network. Serviceability is measured from active collection points.
   132	- **Transfer point / hub** — where a sample changes custody or moves between transport legs.
   133	- **Laboratory** — where a sample is received and its journey completes; a laboratory accepts specific sample types.
   134	
   135	A location may perform several of these functions at the same time.
   136	
   137	## Journey and assignment rules
   138	
   139	The system must support direct, multi-stop and batched journeys.
   140	
   141	A journey may contain several separately assigned transport legs. For example:
   142	
   143	1. Patient’s home to a local collection centre
   144	2. Local collection centre to a hub
   145	3. Hub to the laboratory
   146	
   147	Each movement between two locations is a separate assignment and may be handled by a different worker.
   148

While a new serviceability-calculation version is being computed, the system must keep serving the previous complete serviceability-calculation version, so that no request is checked against a partial or in-progress calculation.

   155	A batch is valid only when:
   156	
   157	- The assigned worker is eligible.
   158	- The samples are allowed to travel together.
   159	- Their container and temperature requirements are compatible.
   160	- Enough capacity is available.
   161	- Stops are in the correct order.

   163	
   164	Whenever a route or batch changes, validate every affected leg and capacity reservation against these same criteria. If that validation fails, reject the change and keep the current plan in place.
   165	
   166	## Capacity
   167	
   168	Collection nodes, laboratories and transport connections may have separate regular and cooled capacity, tracked as configured, reserved, and available units for both regular and cooled storage or transport.
   169	
   170	Capacity must be reserved when a journey is created and released when it is no longer required. The system must never overbook a capacity pool.
   171	
   172	## Chain of custody
   173	
   174	Every sealed sample must have exactly one current holder at all times.
   175	
   176	A handoff requires confirmation from both the sender and receiver. Until both sides confirm, the sender remains responsible for the sample. The receiver becomes the current holder only after the handoff is complete. Repeated or delayed handoff confirmations must not create duplicate transfers of custody. All custody changes must appear in the sample’s lifecycle and audit history. 
   177	
   178	At any point while holding custody of a sample, a certified collection professional, relay courier, node handler, or laboratory intake operator may record a handling checkpoint - the container type and temperature they currently observe. If the observed container or temperature falls outside the sample's required range, the sample must be marked as an exception.
   179	
   180	## Disruptions and replanning
   181	
   182	When part of a journey becomes unavailable:
   183	
   184	- Keep the current sample holder unchanged.
   185	- Preserve completed assignments, stops and handoffs.
   186	- Replan only unfinished work.
   187	- Allow only one active replacement plan.
   188	- Recheck worker eligibility, compatibility, capacity and deadlines.
   189	- Mark the sample as expired if no valid route can meet its deadline.
   190	
   191	Plan changes must use journey plan-version checks so that outdated updates cannot overwrite newer ones for that journey.
   192	
   193	## Tracking and audit
   194	
   195	Show routes, nodes, laboratories, and the current locations of certified collection professionals and relay couriers on a live map.
   196	
   197	For each sample, show:

   199	- Its current or last known location

   201	- Route progress
   202	- The time of its last update
   203	- Whether that location is stale

Each audit record must capture the user, their role, the action taken, the affected item, the time, the outcome, and the relevant changes.

import json
with open('/workspace/contracts/openapi.contract.json') as f:
    spec = json.load(f)

# dump request bodies and 2xx response data schemas for key ops
ops = [
    '/api/authenticate-user',
    '/api/select-active-role',
    '/api/create-user',
    '/api/update-user-access',
    '/api/create-location',
    '/api/update-location',
    '/api/set-location-status',
    '/api/set-location-function-status',
    '/api/create-connection',
    '/api/set-connection-status',
    '/api/configure-capacity',
    '/api/configure-laboratory-acceptance',
    '/api/create-sample-type',
    '/api/update-sample-type',
    '/api/check-serviceability',
    '/api/read-serviceability-snapshot',
    '/api/create-collection-request',
    '/api/ingest-presealed-sample',
    '/api/read-sample-lifecycle',
    '/api/list-role-work',
    '/api/accept-assignment',
    '/api/decline-assignment',
    '/api/collect-and-seal-sample',
    '/api/record-worker-location',
    '/api/update-assignment-progress',
    '/api/initiate-handoff',
    '/api/confirm-handoff',
    '/api/record-handling-checkpoint',
    '/api/confirm-laboratory-receipt',
    '/api/record-laboratory-exception',
    '/api/set-worker-availability',
    '/api/read-journey-plan',
    '/api/edit-active-plan',
    '/api/split-journey',
    '/api/merge-journeys',
    '/api/cancel-journey',
    '/api/reroute-journey',
    '/api/report-disruption',
    '/api/read-operations-state',
    '/api/search-audit-trail',
]

for path in ops:
    methods = spec['paths'][path]
    for method, op in methods.items():
        print(f'\n######## {method.upper()} {path} ({op.get("operationId")}) ########')
        rb = op.get('requestBody')
        if rb:
            schema = rb['content']['application/json']['schema']
            print('REQUEST required:', schema.get('required'))
            print('REQUEST props:', list(schema.get('properties',{}).keys()))
            # print extra details for nested
            for k,v in schema.get('properties',{}).items():
                extra = ''
                if 'enum' in v: extra = f' enum={v["enum"]}'
                if '$ref' in v: extra = f' ref={v["$ref"]}'
                if v.get('type')=='object' and 'properties' in v:
                    extra = f' nested={list(v["properties"].keys())} req={v.get("required")}'
                if 'allOf' in v:
                    extra = ' allOf'
                print(f'  {k}: {v.get("type","?")}{extra}')
        for code in ['200','201']:
            if code in op.get('responses',{}):
                content = op['responses'][code].get('content',{}).get('application/json',{})
                schema = content.get('schema',{})
                data = schema.get('properties',{}).get('data',{})
                print(f'RESPONSE {code} data required:', data.get('required'))
                print(f'RESPONSE {code} data props:', list(data.get('properties',{}).keys()) if 'properties' in data else data.get('$ref','?'))
                if 'properties' in data:
                    for k,v in data.get('properties',{}).items():
                        extra = ''
                        if 'enum' in v: extra = f' enum={v["enum"]}'
                        print(f'  {k}: {v.get("type","?")}{extra}')

print('\n=== SampleState full ===')
print(json.dumps(spec['components']['schemas']['SampleState'], indent=2)[:6000])

print('\n=== SampleLifecycle full ===')
print(json.dumps(spec['components']['schemas']['SampleLifecycle'], indent=2)[:4000])

print('\n=== JourneyPlan ===')
print(json.dumps(spec['components']['schemas']['JourneyPlan'], indent=2)[:4000])

print('\n=== OperationsState required ===')
print(spec['components']['schemas']['OperationsState'].get('required'))
print(list(spec['components']['schemas']['OperationsState']['properties'].keys()))

print('\n=== Capacity ===')
print(json.dumps(spec['components']['schemas']['Capacity'], indent=2))

print('\n=== AuditSearchResult ===')
print(json.dumps(spec['components']['schemas']['AuditSearchResult'], indent=2)[:2500])

print('\n=== TimelineEntry ===')
print(json.dumps(spec['components']['schemas']['TimelineEntry'], indent=2))

print('\n=== Role enum ===')
print(json.dumps(spec['components']['schemas']['Role'], indent=2))

import json
with open('/workspace/contracts/openapi.contract.json') as f:
    spec = json.load(f)

# remaining ops that were clipped
ops = [
    '/api/check-serviceability',
    '/api/read-serviceability-snapshot',
    '/api/create-collection-request',
    '/api/ingest-presealed-sample',
    '/api/read-sample-lifecycle',
    '/api/list-role-work',
    '/api/accept-assignment',
    '/api/decline-assignment',
    '/api/collect-and-seal-sample',
    '/api/record-worker-location',
    '/api/update-assignment-progress',
    '/api/initiate-handoff',
    '/api/confirm-handoff',
    '/api/record-handling-checkpoint',
    '/api/confirm-laboratory-receipt',
    '/api/read-sample-state/{sampleId}',
    '/api/read-user/{userId}',
    '/ready',
    '/api/events',
]

for path in ops:
    methods = spec['paths'][path]
    for method, op in methods.items():
        print(f'\n######## {method.upper()} {path} ({op.get("operationId")}) ########')
        rb = op.get('requestBody')
        if rb:
            schema = rb['content']['application/json']['schema']
            print('REQUEST required:', schema.get('required'))
            print('REQUEST props:', list(schema.get('properties',{}).keys()))
            for k,v in schema.get('properties',{}).items():
                extra = ''
                if 'enum' in v: extra = f' enum={v["enum"]}'
                if '$ref' in v: extra = f' ref={v["$ref"]}'
                if v.get('type')=='object' and 'properties' in v:
                    extra = f' nested={list(v["properties"].keys())} req={v.get("required")}'
                if 'allOf' in v: extra = ' allOf'
                print(f'  {k}: {v.get("type","?")}{extra}')
        params = op.get('parameters', [])
        if params:
            print('PARAMS:', [(p.get('name'), p.get('in'), p.get('required')) for p in params])
        for code in ['200','201']:
            if code in op.get('responses',{}):
                content = op['responses'][code].get('content',{}).get('application/json',{})
                schema = content.get('schema',{})
                data = schema.get('properties',{}).get('data',{})
                print(f'RESPONSE {code} data required:', data.get('required'))
                print(f'RESPONSE {code} data props:', list(data.get('properties',{}).keys()) if 'properties' in data else data.get('$ref','?'))
                if 'properties' in data:
                    for k,v in data.get('properties',{}).items():
                        extra = ''
                        if 'enum' in v: extra = f' enum={v["enum"]}'
                        if '$ref' in v: extra = f' ref={v["$ref"]}'
                        if v.get('type')=='object' and 'properties' in v:
                            extra = f' nested={list(v["properties"].keys())} req={v.get("required")}'
                        print(f'  {k}: {v.get("type","?")}{extra}')

print('\n=== JourneyPlan / WorkerJourneyPlan / RequesterJourneyPlan ===')
for name in ['JourneyPlan','WorkerJourneyPlan','RequesterJourneyPlan']:
    s = spec['components']['schemas'][name]
    print(name, 'required:', s.get('required'))
    print('  props:', list(s['properties'].keys()))

print('\n=== AuditEntry ===')
print(json.dumps(spec['components']['schemas']['AuditEntry'], indent=2)[:2500])

print('\n=== OperationsState full (minus samples/workers already seen) ===')
ops = spec['components']['schemas']['OperationsState']['properties']
for k in ['locations','connections','routes','handoffs','delays','exceptions','assignmentCountSpread','ineligibleAssignmentCount']:
    print(f'\n--- {k} ---')
    print(json.dumps(ops[k], indent=2)[:2000])

print('\n=== read-sample-lifecycle request ===')
print(json.dumps(spec['paths']['/api/read-sample-lifecycle']['post'].get('requestBody'), indent=2)[:2000])

print('\n=== read-sample-state path params ===')
print(json.dumps(spec['paths']['/api/read-sample-state/{sampleId}']['get'].get('parameters'), indent=2))

print('\n=== list-role-work 200 ===')
print(json.dumps(spec['paths']['/api/list-role-work']['post']['responses']['200']['content']['application/json']['schema'], indent=2)[:2000])

print('\n=== authenticate 401/409 codes ===')
for code in ['400','401','409']:
    r = spec['paths']['/api/authenticate-user']['post']['responses'].get(code,{})
    print(code, json.dumps(r.get('content',{}).get('application/json',{}).get('schema',{}), indent=2)[:800])

print('\n=== ErrorEnvelope ===')
print(json.dumps(spec['components']['schemas']['ErrorEnvelope'], indent=2))

     1	# Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System
     2	
     3	Clinical samples may start at a patient’s home, a clinic, or a collection point and must reach a suitable laboratory before their delivery deadline.
     4	
     5	Home samples must be collected and sealed by a certified collection professional before they can enter the transport network. Once sealed, a sample may pass through relay couriers, collection centres and hubs before reaching the laboratory.
     6	
     7	Dispatchers currently coordinate much of this work through calls, chat groups, and spreadsheets. This makes it difficult to track custody, use available capacity, assign work fairly, combine compatible samples, and recover when part of the network becomes unavailable.
     8	
     9	Build a web application that manages this entire process, from the initial serviceability check through laboratory receipt.
    10	
    11	## Users and responsibilities
    12	
    13	Use role-based access control for both actions and data: each user may perform actions and see data only as permitted by the role or roles they currently hold.
    14	
    15	For each of their roles, a user can see their current work and their past (completed) work, and can view a status timeline — the ordered history of status changes — for every item of work they are responsible for.
    16	
    17	A user may have more than one assigned role:
    18	
    19	- The user must explicitly select the role they are currently working under, and permissions and work views must use that selected role.
    20	- Switching role context must not add or remove any roles from the account.
    21	
    22	### Requester
    23	
    24	A requester should be able to:
    25	
    26	- Check whether a location and sample can be serviced before creating a request.
    27	- Create a home or clinic collection request.
    28	- Follow the sample’s current status, location, route and history.
    29	- See only requests that belong to them.
    30	
    31	The serviceability check must be a dry run. It must not create a request, sample, journey, assignment or capacity reservation.
    32	
    33	### Certified collection professional
    34	
    35	A certified collection professional should be able to:
    36	
    37	- View collection work for which they are qualified.
    38	- Accept or decline an offered collection assignment.
    39	- Record that a sample was collected and sealed.
    40	- Record their current location.
    41	- Hand off and confirm the transfer of the sealed sample to a relay courier or facility.
    42	
    43	### Relay courier
    44	
    45	A relay courier should be able to:
    46	
    47	- View delivery work assigned to them.
    48	- Accept or decline an offered transport assignment.
    49	- See only the details needed for their assigned leg.
    50	- Record location and progress updates.
    51	- Confirm pickup and handoff with the other party.
    52	
    53	### Node handler
    54	
    55	A node handler should be able to:
    56	
    57	- Accept or decline an offered node assignment.
    58	- Manage samples arriving at and leaving a collection centre or hub.
    59	- Register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system.
    60	- Confirm incoming and outgoing handoffs.
    61	- View and configure regular and cooled capacity at the node they are assigned to.
    62	
    63	### Laboratory intake operator
    64	
    65	A laboratory intake operator should be able to:
    66	
    67	- Accept or decline an offered laboratory assignment.
    68	- View expected samples and configure regular and cooled capacity at the laboratory they are assigned to.
    69	- Confirm that a sample was received.
    70	- Record an exception when a sample cannot be accepted normally.
    71	
    72	### Dispatcher
    73	
    74	A dispatcher should be able to:
    75	
    76	- Monitor samples, workers, collection nodes, laboratories, routes and exceptions.
    77	- See the current holder of each sample and whether its latest location is stale.
    78	- View the full journey, including collection and individual transport legs.
    79	- Change, split, merge, cancel or reroute unfinished work.
    80	- Replan unfinished work when a worker, node, route, laboratory or capacity pool becomes unavailable.
    81	- Search the complete audit history of a request or sample.
    82	
    83	Completed work and confirmed custody must not be rewritten during replanning.
    84	
    85	### Administrator
    86	
    87	An administrator may also do everything a dispatcher can do.
    88	
    89	In addition, only an administrator can:
    90	
    91	- Manage users, roles and professional certifications, including which node or laboratory a node handler or laboratory intake operator is assigned to.
    92	- Create and update collection nodes and laboratories.
    93	- Create and update sample types and their handling attributes.
    94	- Activate or deactivate a location, an individual function it provides, or a connection, without restarting the application.
    95	- Configure service coverage, travel times, handling times and laboratory capabilities.
    96	- Configure regular and cooled capacity for any node, laboratory, or transport connection.
    97	
    98	## Collection requests
    99	
   100	A collection request records where and when a sample can be collected and when it must reach the laboratory:
   101	
   102	- **Origin** — a patient’s home, a clinic, or a network node.
   103	- **Sample type** — see Sample types below.
   104	- **Collection window** — the earliest and latest time at which the sample may be collected. Collection must take place inside this window.
   105	- **Delivery deadline** — the time by which the sample must be received at the laboratory.
   106	
   107	The collection window and the delivery deadline are separate constraints: the window governs when pickup may happen, the deadline governs when laboratory receipt must happen. A plan is valid only when collection takes place within the collection window and the sample can still reach an accepting laboratory before its delivery deadline.
   108	
   109	## Pre-sealed samples
   110	
   111	A certified collection professional, relay courier, node handler, or laboratory intake operator may register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system — the person registering it must be the one who currently holds it.
   112	
   113	- Its origin must be a clinic or a network node — not a home.
   114	- The system should create only the transport legs needed from the point of registration onward.
   115	
   116	## Sample types
   117	
   118	Every sample has a type that determines its handling rules, and those rules apply for the whole journey, from collection through laboratory receipt. The system must have at least the following named types available by default: Amber, Indigo, Frost, Pulse. Each of the four requires a qualified collector — only a certified collection professional holding the matching qualification may collect it.
   119	
   120	- **Amber** — standard handling.
   121	- **Indigo** — must not share a container with an Amber sample.
   122	- **Frost** — requires cooled storage and transport throughout its entire journey.
   123	- **Pulse** — time-critical; it must not wait to be combined into a consolidation batch and must be routed without batching delay.
   124	
   125	These named rules are in addition to the generic handling attributes (container, temperature range, qualified-collector requirement, and incompatibilities).
   126	
   127	## Network locations
   128	
   129	The transport network is made up of locations. A single location — a node — may act as a collection point, a transfer point, a hub, a laboratory, or any combination of these (for example, a hub that also acts as a laboratory).
   130	
   131	- **Collection point** — where samples are collected from or enter the network. Serviceability is measured from active collection points.
   132	- **Transfer point / hub** — where a sample changes custody or moves between transport legs.
   133	- **Laboratory** — where a sample is received and its journey completes; a laboratory accepts specific sample types.
   134	
   135	A location may perform several of these functions at the same time.
   136	
   137	## Journey and assignment rules
   138	
   139	The system must support direct, multi-stop and batched journeys.
   140	
   141	A journey may contain several separately assigned transport legs. For example:
   142	
   143	1. Patient’s home to a local collection centre
   144	2. Local collection centre to a hub
   145	3. Hub to the laboratory
   146	
   147	Each movement between two locations is a separate assignment and may be handled by a different worker.
   148	
   149	Collection must happen before transport. Pickup must happen before delivery, and responsibility for the sample must be transferred through a confirmed handoff before the next person continues the journey.

USER_CONTEXT: Implement full-stack Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System matching pinned OpenAPI + UI contracts. Clinical samples (home/clinic/collection point) must reach a lab before deadline; home samples require certified collector sealing before transport; then relay via couriers/centres/hubs. Stack: Go backend + React/Vite frontend + schemas. Handoff requires both-side confirmation; sender remains responsible until complete; no duplicate custody transfers; all custody changes on sample timeline.

COMPLETED: Explored existing codebase to map contract gaps (backend handlers, schemas, frontend scaffold, UI contract, map assets). No implementation edits yet.

PENDING: Align backend responses with OpenAPI (routes, status codes, response shapes); complete/build frontend to match UI contract scenarios; implement app-setup; close remaining API/UI gaps.

     1	# Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System
     2	
     3	Clinical samples may start at a patient’s home, a clinic, or a collection point and must reach a suitable laboratory before their delivery deadline.
     4	
     5	Home samples must be collected and sealed by a certified collection professional before they can enter the transport network. Once sealed, a sample may pass through relay couriers, collection centres and hubs before reaching the laboratory.
     6	
     7	Dispatchers currently coordinate much of this work through calls, chat groups, and spreadsheets. This makes it difficult to track custody, use available capacity, assign work fairly, combine compatible samples, and recover when part of the network becomes unavailable.
     8	
     9	Build a web application that manages this entire process, from the initial serviceability check through laboratory receipt.
    10	
    11	## Users and responsibilities
    12	
    13	Use role-based access control for both actions and data: each user may perform actions and see data only as permitted by the role or roles they currently hold.
    14	
    15	For each of their roles, a user can see their current work and their past (completed) work, and can view a status timeline — the ordered history of status changes — for every item of work they are responsible for.
    16	
    17	A user may have more than one assigned role:
    18	
    19	- The user must explicitly select the role they are currently working under, and permissions and work views must use that selected role.
    20	- Switching role context must not add or remove any roles from the account.
    21	
    22	### Requester
    23	
    24	A requester should be able to:
    25	
    26	- Check whether a location and sample can be serviced before creating a request.
    27	- Create a home or clinic collection request.
    28	- Follow the sample’s current status, location, route and history.
    29	- See only requests that belong to them.
    30	
    31	The serviceability check must be a dry run. It must not create a request, sample, journey, assignment or capacity reservation.
    32	
    33	### Certified collection professional
    34	
    35	A certified collection professional should be able to:
    36	
    37	- View collection work for which they are qualified.
    38	- Accept or decline an offered collection assignment.
    39	- Record that a sample was collected and sealed.
    40	- Record their current location.
    41	- Hand off and confirm the transfer of the sealed sample to a relay courier or facility.
    42	
    43	### Relay courier
    44	
    45	A relay courier should be able to:
    46	
    47	- View delivery work assigned to them.
    48	- Accept or decline an offered transport assignment.
    49	- See only the details needed for their assigned leg.
    50	- Record location and progress updates.
    51	- Confirm pickup and handoff with the other party.
    52	
    53	### Node handler
    54	
    55	A node handler should be able to:
    56	
    57	- Accept or decline an offered node assignment.
    58	- Manage samples arriving at and leaving a collection centre or hub.
    59	- Register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system.
    60	- Confirm incoming and outgoing handoffs.
    61	- View and configure regular and cooled capacity at the node they are assigned to.
    62	
    63	### Laboratory intake operator
    64	
    65	A laboratory intake operator should be able to:
    66	
    67	- Accept or decline an offered laboratory assignment.
    68	- View expected samples and configure regular and cooled capacity at the laboratory they are assigned to.
    69	- Confirm that a sample was received.
    70	- Record an exception when a sample cannot be accepted normally.
    71	
    72	### Dispatcher
    73	
    74	A dispatcher should be able to:
    75	
    76	- Monitor samples, workers, collection nodes, laboratories, routes and exceptions.
    77	- See the current holder of each sample and whether its latest location is stale.
    78	- View the full journey, including collection and individual transport legs.
    79	- Change, split, merge, cancel or reroute unfinished work.
    80	- Replan unfinished work when a worker, node, route, laboratory or capacity pool becomes unavailable.

     2	
     3	Clinical samples may start at a patient’s home, a clinic, or a collection point and must reach a suitable laboratory before their delivery deadline.
     4	
     5	Home samples must be collected and sealed by a certified collection professional before they can enter the transport network. Once sealed, a sample may pass through relay couriers, collection centres and hubs before reaching the laboratory.
     6

python3 << 'PY'
import json
p="/workspace/contracts/openapi.contract.json"
with open(p) as f:
    d=json.load(f)

# Remaining ops request/response
ops = ["create_collection_request","check_serviceability","decline_assignment",
       "collect_and_seal_sample","initiate_handoff","confirm_handoff","confirm_laboratory_receipt",
       "record_laboratory_exception","record_handling_checkpoint",
       "create_location","create_user","create_sample_type",
       "ingest_presealed_sample","read_sample_lifecycle","read_journey_plan",
       "list_role_work","cancel_journey","reroute_journey","report_disruption","edit_active_plan",
       "split_journey","merge_journeys","set_worker_availability","configure_laboratory_acceptance",
       "create_connection","record_worker_location","search_audit_trail",
       "authenticate_user","select_active_role","set_location_status","set_location_function_status",
       "set_connection_status","configure_capacity"]
for path, methods in d["paths"].items():
    for m, op in methods.items():
        if m.startswith("x-"): continue
        oid = op.get("operationId")
        if oid not in ops:
            continue
        print("="*70)
        print(oid, m.upper(), path)
        rb = op.get("requestBody")
        if rb:
            content = rb.get("content",{})
            for ct, body in content.items():
                schema = body.get("schema",{})
                print("REQUEST required:", schema.get("required"))
                print("REQUEST props:", list(schema.get("properties",{}).keys()) if "properties" in schema else schema)
        print("SUCCESS:")
        for code, resp in op.get("responses",{}).items():
            if code.startswith("2"):
                content = resp.get("content",{})
                for ct, body in content.items():
                    schema = body.get("schema",{})
                    data = schema.get("properties",{}).get("data", schema)
                    print(f"  {code} required:", data.get("required") if isinstance(data, dict) else data)
                    if isinstance(data, dict) and "properties" in data:
                        print(f"  {code} props:", list(data["properties"].keys()))
                    elif isinstance(data, dict) and "$ref" in data:
                        print(f"  {code} ref:", data["$ref"])
        print("ERROR codes:")
        for code, resp in op.get("responses",{}).items():
            if code.startswith("4") or code.startswith("5"):
                content = resp.get("content",{})
                for ct, body in content.items():
                    schema = body.get("schema",{})
                    codes = schema.get("properties",{}).get("code",{}).get("enum",[])
                    if codes:
                        print(f"  {code}: {codes}")
PY

     1	# Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System
     2	
     3	Clinical samples may start at a patient’s home, a clinic, or a collection point and must reach a suitable laboratory before their delivery deadline.
     4	
     5	Home samples must be collected and sealed by a certified collection professional before they can enter the transport network. Once sealed, a sample may pass through relay couriers, collection centres and hubs before reaching the laboratory.
     6	
     7	Dispatchers currently coordinate much of this work through calls, chat groups, and spreadsheets. This makes it difficult to track custody, use available capacity, assign work fairly, combine compatible samples, and recover when part of the network becomes unavailable.
     8	
     9	Build a web application that manages this entire process, from the initial serviceability check through laboratory receipt.
    10	
    11	## Users and responsibilities
    12	
    13	Use role-based access control for both actions and data: each user may perform actions and see data only as permitted by the role or roles they currently hold.
    14	
    15	For each of their roles, a user can see their current work and their past (completed) work, and can view a status timeline — the ordered history of status changes — for every item of work they are responsible for.
    16	
    17	A user may have more than one assigned role:
    18	
    19	- The user must explicitly select the role they are currently working under, and permissions and work views must use that selected role.
    20	- Switching role context must not add or remove any roles from the account.
    21	
    22	### Requester
    23	
    24	A requester should be able to:
    25	
    26	- Check whether a location and sample can be serviced before creating a request.
    27	- Create a home or clinic collection request.
    28	- Follow the sample’s current status, location, route and history.
    29	- See only requests that belong to them.
    30	
    31	The serviceability check must be a dry run. It must not create a request, sample, journey, assignment or capacity reservation.
    32	
    33	### Certified collection professional
    34	
    35	A certified collection professional should be able to:
    36	
    37	- View collection work for which they are qualified.
    38	- Accept or decline an offered collection assignment.
    39	- Record that a sample was collected and sealed.
    40	- Record their current location.
    41	- Hand off and confirm the transfer of the sealed sample to a relay courier or facility.
    42	
    43	### Relay courier
    44	
    45	A relay courier should be able to:
    46	
    47	- View delivery work assigned to them.
    48	- Accept or decline an offered transport assignment.
    49	- See only the details needed for their assigned leg.
    50	- Record location and progress updates.
    51	- Confirm pickup and handoff with the other party.
    52	
    53	### Node handler
    54	
    55	A node handler should be able to:
    56	
    57	- Accept or decline an offered node assignment.
    58	- Manage samples arriving at and leaving a collection centre or hub.
    59	- Register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system.
    60	- Confirm incoming and outgoing handoffs.
    61	- View and configure regular and cooled capacity at the node they are assigned to.
    62	
    63	### Laboratory intake operator
    64	
    65	A laboratory intake operator should be able to:
    66	
    67	- Accept or decline an offered laboratory assignment.
    68	- View expected samples and configure regular and cooled capacity at the laboratory they are assigned to.
    69	- Confirm that a sample was received.
    70	- Record an exception when a sample cannot be accepted normally.
    71	
    72	### Dispatcher
    73	
    74	A dispatcher should be able to:
    75	
    76	- Monitor samples, workers, collection nodes, laboratories, routes and exceptions.
    77	- See the current holder of each sample and whether its latest location is stale.
    78	- View the full journey, including collection and individual transport legs.
    79	- Change, split, merge, cancel or reroute unfinished work.
    80	- Replan unfinished work when a worker, node, route, laboratory or capacity pool becomes unavailable.
    81	- Search the complete audit history of a request or sample.
    82	
    83	Completed work and confirmed custody must not be rewritten during replanning.
    84	
    85	### Administrator
    86	
    87	An administrator may also do everything a dispatcher can do.
    88	
    89	In addition, only an administrator can:
    90	
    91	- Manage users, roles and professional certifications, including which node or laboratory a node handler or laboratory intake operator is assigned to.
    92	- Create and update collection nodes and laboratories.
    93	- Create and update sample types and their handling attributes.
    94	- Activate or deactivate a location, an individual function it provides, or a connection, without restarting the application.
    95	- Configure service coverage, travel times, handling times and laboratory capabilities.
    96	- Configure regular and cooled capacity for any node, laboratory, or transport connection.
    97	
    98	## Collection requests
    99	
   100	A collection request records where and when a sample can be collected and when it must reach the laboratory:
   101	
   102	- **Origin** — a patient’s home, a clinic, or a network node.
   103	- **Sample type** — see Sample types below.
   104	- **Collection window** — the earliest and latest time at which the sample may be collected. Collection must take place inside this window.
   105	- **Delivery deadline** — the time by which the sample must be received at the laboratory.
   106	
   107	The collection window and the delivery deadline are separate constraints: the window governs when pickup may happen, the deadline governs when laboratory receipt must happen. A plan is valid only when collection takes place within the collection window and the sample can still reach an accepting laboratory before its delivery deadline.
   108	
   109	## Pre-sealed samples
   110	
   111	A certified collection professional, relay courier, node handler, or laboratory intake operator may register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system — the person registering it must be the one who currently holds it.
   112	
   113	- Its origin must be a clinic or a network node — not a home.
   114	- The system should create only the transport legs needed from the point of registration onward.
   115	
   116	## Sample types
   117	
   118	Every sample has a type that determines its handling rules, and those rules apply for the whole journey, from collection through laboratory receipt. The system must have at least the following named types available by default: Amber, Indigo, Frost, Pulse. Each of the four requires a qualified collector — only a certified collection professional holding the matching qualification may collect it.
   119	
   120	- **Amber** — standard handling.
   121	- **Indigo** — must not share a container with an Amber sample.
   122	- **Frost** — requires cooled storage and transport throughout its entire journey.
   123	- **Pulse** — time-critical; it must not wait to be combined into a consolidation batch and must be routed without batching delay.
   124	
   125	These named rules are in addition to the generic handling attributes (container, temperature range, qualified-collector requirement, and incompatibilities).
   126	
   127	## Network locations
   128	
   129	The transport network is made up of locations. A single location — a node — may act as a collection point, a transfer point, a hub, a laboratory, or any combination of these (for example, a hub that also acts as a laboratory).
   130	
   131	- **Collection point** — where samples are collected from or enter the network. Serviceability is measured from active collection points.
   132	- **Transfer point / hub** — where a sample changes custody or moves between transport legs.
   133	- **Laboratory** — where a sample is received and its journey completes; a laboratory accepts specific sample types.
   134	
   135	A location may perform several of these functions at the same time.
   136	
   137	## Journey and assignment rules
   138	
   139	The system must support direct, multi-stop and batched journeys.
   140	
   141	A journey may contain several separately assigned transport legs. For example:
   142	
   143	1. Patient’s home to a local collection centre
   144	2. Local collection centre to a hub
   145	3. Hub to the laboratory
   146	
   147	Each movement between two locations is a separate assignment and may be handled by a different worker.
   148	
   149	Collection must happen before transport. Pickup must happen before delivery, and responsibility for the sample must be transferred through a confirmed handoff before the next person continues the journey.

        print("="*70)
        print(oid, m.upper(), path)
        print("params:", json.dumps(op.get("parameters",[]), indent=2)[:1500])
        rb = op.get("requestBody")
        if rb:
            content = rb.get("content",{})
            for ct, body in content.items():
                schema = body.get("schema",{})
                print("REQUEST required:", schema.get("required"))
                print("REQUEST props:", list(schema.get("properties",{}).keys()) if "properties" in schema else json.dumps(schema)[:1500])
        print("SUCCESS:")
        for code, resp in op.get("responses",{}).items():
            if code.startswith("2"):
                content = resp.get("content",{})
                for ct, body in content.items():
                    schema = body.get("schema",{})
                    print(f"  {code}:", json.dumps(schema, indent=2)[:2500])

Domain: clinical samples (home/clinic/collection point) must reach a lab before deadline; home samples require certified collector sealing; relay via couriers/centres/hubs. Handoff requires both-side confirmation; sender remains responsible until complete; no duplicate custody transfers; all custody changes on sample timeline.

- Align remaining Go handlers to pinned OpenAPI response/request shapes (IN PROGRESS)
- Build React/Vite frontend matching ui.contract.json scenarios (PENDING)
- Produce handoff artifacts (PENDING)

     1	# Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System
     2	
     3	Clinical samples may start at a patient’s home, a clinic, or a collection point and must reach a suitable laboratory before their delivery deadline.
     4	
     5	Home samples must be collected and sealed by a certified collection professional before they can enter the transport network. Once sealed, a sample may pass through relay couriers, collection centres and hubs before reaching the laboratory.
     6	
     7	Dispatchers currently coordinate much of this work through calls, chat groups, and spreadsheets. This makes it difficult to track custody, use available capacity, assign work fairly, combine compatible samples, and recover when part of the network becomes unavailable.
     8	
     9	Build a web application that manages this entire process, from the initial serviceability check through laboratory receipt.
    10	
    11	## Users and responsibilities
    12	
    13	Use role-based access control for both actions and data: each user may perform actions and see data only as permitted by the role or roles they currently hold.
    14	
    15	For each of their roles, a user can see their current work and their past (completed) work, and can view a status timeline — the ordered history of status changes — for every item of work they are responsible for.
    16	
    17	A user may have more than one assigned role:
    18	
    19	- The user must explicitly select the role they are currently working under, and permissions and work views must use that selected role.
    20	- Switching role context must not add or remove any roles from the account.
    21	
    22	### Requester
    23	
    24	A requester should be able to:
    25	
    26	- Check whether a location and sample can be serviced before creating a request.
    27	- Create a home or clinic collection request.
    28	- Follow the sample’s current status, location, route and history.
    29	- See only requests that belong to them.
    30	
    31	The serviceability check must be a dry run. It must not create a request, sample, journey, assignment or capacity reservation.
    32	
    33	### Certified collection professional
    34	
    35	A certified collection professional should be able to:
    36	
    37	- View collection work for which they are qualified.
    38	- Accept or decline an offered collection assignment.
    39	- Record that a sample was collected and sealed.
    40	- Record their current location.
    41	- Hand off and confirm the transfer of the sealed sample to a relay courier or facility.
    42	
    43	### Relay courier
    44	
    45	A relay courier should be able to:
    46	
    47	- View delivery work assigned to them.
    48	- Accept or decline an offered transport assignment.
    49	- See only the details needed for their assigned leg.
    50	- Record location and progress updates.
    51	- Confirm pickup and handoff with the other party.
    52	
    53	### Node handler
    54	
    55	A node handler should be able to:
    56	
    57	- Accept or decline an offered node assignment.
    58	- Manage samples arriving at and leaving a collection centre or hub.
    59	- Register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system.
    60	- Confirm incoming and outgoing handoffs.
    61	- View and configure regular and cooled capacity at the node they are assigned to.
    62	
    63	### Laboratory intake operator
    64	
    65	A laboratory intake operator should be able to:
    66	
    67	- Accept or decline an offered laboratory assignment.
    68	- View expected samples and configure regular and cooled capacity at the laboratory they are assigned to.
    69	- Confirm that a sample was received.
    70	- Record an exception when a sample cannot be accepted normally.
    71	
    72	### Dispatcher
    73	
    74	A dispatcher should be able to:
    75	
    76	- Monitor samples, workers, collection nodes, laboratories, routes and exceptions.
    77	- See the current holder of each sample and whether its latest location is stale.
    78	- View the full journey, including collection and individual transport legs.
    79	- Change, split, merge, cancel or reroute unfinished work.
    80	- Replan unfinished work when a worker, node, route, laboratory or capacity pool becomes unavailable.
    81	- Search the complete audit history of a request or sample.
    82	
    83	Completed work and confirmed custody must not be rewritten during replanning.
    84	
    85	### Administrator
    86	
    87	An administrator may also do everything a dispatcher can do.
    88	
    89	In addition, only an administrator can:
    90	
    91	- Manage users, roles and professional certifications, including which node or laboratory a node handler or laboratory intake operator is assigned to.
    92	- Create and update collection nodes and laboratories.
    93	- Create and update sample types and their handling attributes.
    94	- Activate or deactivate a location, an individual function it provides, or a connection, without restarting the application.
    95	- Configure service coverage, travel times, handling times and laboratory capabilities.
    96	- Configure regular and cooled capacity for any node, laboratory, or transport connection.
    97	
    98	## Collection requests
    99	
   100	A collection request records where and when a sample can be collected and when it must reach the laboratory:
   101	
   102	- **Origin** — a patient’s home, a clinic, or a network node.
   103	- **Sample type** — see Sample types below.
   104	- **Collection window** — the earliest and latest time at which the sample may be collected. Collection must take place inside this window.
   105	- **Delivery deadline** — the time by which the sample must be received at the laboratory.
   106	
   107	The collection window and the delivery deadline are separate constraints: the window governs when pickup may happen, the deadline governs when laboratory receipt must happen. A plan is valid only when collection takes place within the collection window and the sample can still reach an accepting laboratory before its delivery deadline.
   108	
   109	## Pre-sealed samples
   110	
   111	A certified collection professional, relay courier, node handler, or laboratory intake operator may register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system — the person registering it must be the one who currently holds it.
   112	
   113	- Its origin must be a clinic or a network node — not a home.
   114	- The system should create only the transport legs needed from the point of registration onward.
   115	
   116	## Sample types
   117	
   118	Every sample has a type that determines its handling rules, and those rules apply for the whole journey, from collection through laboratory receipt. The system must have at least the following named types available by default: Amber, Indigo, Frost, Pulse. Each of the four requires a qualified collector — only a certified collection professional holding the matching qualification may collect it.
   119	
   120	- **Amber** — standard handling.
   121	- **Indigo** — must not share a container with an Amber sample.
   122	- **Frost** — requires cooled storage and transport throughout its entire journey.
   123	- **Pulse** — time-critical; it must not wait to be combined into a consolidation batch and must be routed without batching delay.
   124	
   125	These named rules are in addition to the generic handling attributes (container, temperature range, qualified-collector requirement, and incompatibilities).
   126	
   127	## Network locations
   128	
   129	The transport network is made up of locations. A single location — a node — may act as a collection point, a transfer point, a hub, a laboratory, or any combination of these (for example, a hub that also acts as a laboratory).
   130	
   131	- **Collection point** — where samples are collected from or enter the network. Serviceability is measured from active collection points.
   132	- **Transfer point / hub** — where a sample changes custody or moves between transport legs.
   133	- **Laboratory** — where a sample is received and its journey completes; a laboratory accepts specific sample types.
   134	
   135	A location may perform several of these functions at the same time.
   136	
   137	## Journey and assignment rules
   138	
   139	The system must support direct, multi-stop and batched journeys.
   140	
   141	A journey may contain several separately assigned transport legs. For example:
   142	
   143	1. Patient’s home to a local collection centre
   144	2. Local collection centre to a hub
   145	3. Hub to the laboratory
   146	
   147	Each movement between two locations is a separate assignment and may be handled by a different worker.
   148	
   149	Collection must happen before transport. Pickup must happen before delivery, and responsibility for the sample must be transferred through a confirmed handoff before the next person continues the journey.
   150

       "record_laboratory_exception","set_worker_availability","read_journey_plan",
       "split_journey","merge_journeys","cancel_journey","reroute_journey","report_disruption",
       "search_audit_trail"]
for path, methods in d["paths"].items():
    for m, op in methods.items():
        if m.startswith("x-"): continue
        oid = op.get("operationId")
        if oid not in ops:
            continue
        print("="*70)
        print(oid, m.upper(), path)
        rb = op.get("requestBody")
        if rb:
            content = rb.get("content",{})
            for ct, body in content.items():
                schema = body.get("schema",{})
                print("  REQ required:", schema.get("required"))
                print("  REQ props:", list(schema.get("properties",{}).keys()) if "properties" in schema else schema)
        print("  RESP:")
        for code, resp in op.get("responses",{}).items():
            if not str(code).startswith("2"):
                continue
            content = resp.get("content",{})
            for ct, body in content.items():
                schema = body.get("schema",{})
                data = schema.get("properties",{}).get("data",{})
                if "$ref" in data:
                    print(f"    {code}: data -> {data['$ref']}")
                elif "properties" in data:
                    print(f"    {code}: data required={data.get('required')} props={list(data.get('properties',{}).keys())}")
                    for k,v in data.get("properties",{}).items():
                        if "properties" in v:

                            print(f"      .{k} -> {v['$ref']}")
                        elif v.get("type")=="array":
                            items=v.get("items",{})
                            print(f"      .{k}[] -> {items.get('$ref', items.get('type'))}")
                else:
                    print(f"    {code}:", json.dumps(schema)[:800])

data.summary:
USER_CONTEXT: Implement full-stack Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System matching pinned OpenAPI + UI contracts. Stack: Go backend + React/Vite frontend + schemas. Domain: clinical samples (home/clinic/collection point) must reach a lab before deadline; home samples require certified collector sealing; relay via couriers/centres/hubs. Handoff requires both-side confirmation; sender remains responsible until complete; no duplicate custody transfers; all custody changes on sample timeline.

TASK_TRACKING:
- Inspect remaining contract/API gaps and align backend response shapes to pinned OpenAPI (IN PROGRESS)
- Implement frontend matching UI contract scenarios (PENDING)
- Produce handoff artifacts (PENDING)

COMPLETED:
- Backend core largely in place (users, assignments, journeys, ws, db, httpx, main)
- Reviewed OpenAPI schemas: OperationsLocation, OperationsConnection, SampleState, RoleWorkItem, SampleWorkItem, JourneyWorkItem, AssignmentWorkItem, TimelineEntry, Capacity, WorkerJourneyPlan, RequesterJourneyPlan, ErrorEnvelope, RealtimeEvent, AuditEntry, JourneyStop, JourneyLeg, RoleWork, SampleLifecycle, Certification
- Reviewed backend files: users.go, assignments.go, ws.go, db.go, journeys.go, util.go, httpx.go, main.go
- Reviewed frontend stubs: tsconfig.json, api.ts, styles.css
- Reviewed contracts/ui.contract.json (scenarios: login_rejects_invalid_credentials, role_switch_control_lists_and_applies_role, role_work_view_shows_current_and_past, sample_view_shows_ordered_status_history, sample_freshness, etc.)
- Reviewed schema/mongo.js and schema/postgres.sql, README.md

PENDING:
- Lock remaining API response shapes to pinned contract (identified mismatches, need to fix handlers)
- Implement full React/Vite frontend for UI contract scenarios
- Handoff artifacts

CURRENT_STATE:
- Backend handlers exist for auth, users, locations, connections, assignments (expireOffers, confirmLabReceipt, etc.), journeys (readJourneyPlan, editActivePlan), worker location, websocket (lab-logistics-v1)
- Store uses Postgres + Mongo (audit_entries)
- Frontend is stub-level (api.ts has SAMPLE_TYPES and ROLES; styles.css theme defined)
- Agent is inspecting remaining handlers and UI contract to close API gaps then build frontend

CODE_STATE:
- /workspace/backend/: main.go, users.go, assignments.go, journeys.go, ws.go, db.go, httpx.go, util.go
- /workspace/frontend/: tsconfig.json, src/api.ts, src/styles.css
- /workspace/contracts/: openapi.contract.json, ui.contract.json
- /workspace/schema/: mongo.js, postgres.sql

DEPS:
- Backend: github.com/gorilla/websocket, github.com/lib/pq, go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver
- Frontend: React/Vite, TypeScript ES2020 bundler resolution

VERSION_CONTROL_STATUS: Working in /workspace; no branch/PR info observed

data.summary:
USER_CONTEXT: Implement full-stack Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System matching pinned OpenAPI + UI contracts. Stack: Go backend + React/Vite frontend + schemas. Domain: clinical samples (home/clinic/collection point) must reach a lab before deadline; home samples require certified collector sealing; relay via couriers/centres/hubs. Handoff requires both-side confirmation; sender remains responsible until complete; no duplicate custody transfers; all custody changes on sample timeline.

TASK_TRACKING:
- Inspect remaining OpenAPI schemas (TimelineEntry, RoleWork, OperationsState) and leftover backend handlers — IN PROGRESS
- Lock backend response shapes to OpenAPI contract — PENDING
- Build React/Vite frontend matching UI contract scenarios — PENDING
- Produce handoff artifacts — PENDING

COMPLETED:
- Explored OpenAPI schemas: TimelineEntry, RoleWork, OperationsState
- Inspected backend handlers: journeys.go (handleMergeJourneys), network.go, requests.go (createRequestBody + materializeJourney), serviceability.go, assignments.go (handleInitiateHandoff), users.go, work.go (handleListRoleWork), auth.go, httpx.go, main.go
- Inspected schemas: postgres.sql, go.mod
- Inspected frontend stubs: api.ts (SAMPLE_TYPES, ROLES), styles.css, package.json, vite.config.ts (proxy /api to :8080), index.html, tsconfig.json
- Inspected UI contract (ui.contract.json v1, product lab-sample-pickup-and-delivery) and workspace layout
- frontend/src currently only has api.ts, styles.css, vite-env.d.ts (no App/main yet)
- app-setup/ is empty

PENDING:
- Finish remaining handler/schema inspection
- Align backend API response shapes to OpenAPI
- Implement full frontend for UI contract scenarios (login_rejects_invalid_credentials, role_switch_control_lists_and_applies_role, role_work_view_shows_current_and_past, sample_view_shows_ordered_status_history, sample_freshnes...)
- Handoff artifacts

CURRENT_STATE:
- Backend: Go 1.22 module lablogistics; deps uuid, gorilla/websocket, lib/pq, mongo-driver, golang.org/x/crypto

     1	# Lab Sample Pickup & Delivery System
     2	
     3	Clinical samples may start at a patient’s home, a clinic, or a collection point and must reach a suitable laboratory before their delivery deadline.
     4	
     5	Home samples must be collected and sealed by a certified collection professional before they can enter the transport network. Once sealed, a sample may pass through relay couriers, collection centres and hubs before reaching the laboratory.
     6	
     7	Dispatchers currently coordinate much of this work through calls, chat groups, and spreadsheets. This makes it difficult to track custody, use available capacity, assign work fairly, combine compatible samples, and recover when part of the network becomes unavailable.
     8	
     9	Build a web application that manages this entire process, from the initial serviceability check through laboratory receipt.
    10	
    11	## Users and responsibilities
    12	
    13	Use role-based access control for both actions and data: each user may perform actions and see data only as permitted by the role or roles they currently hold.
    14	
    15	For each of their roles, a user can see their current work and their past (completed) work, and can view a status timeline — the ordered history of status changes — for every item of work they are responsible for.
    16	
    17	A user may have more than one assigned role:
    18	
    19	- The user must explicitly select the role they are currently working under, and permissions and work views must use that selected role.
    20	- Switching role context must not add or remove any roles from the account.
    21	
    22	### Requester
    23	
    24	A requester should be able to:
    25	
    26	- Check whether a location and sample can be serviced before creating a request.
    27	- Create a home or clinic collection request.
    28	- Follow the sample’s current status, location, route and history.
    29	- See only requests that belong to them.
    30	
    31	The serviceability check must be a dry run. It must not create a request, sample, journey, assignment or capacity reservation.
    32	
    33	### Certified collection professional
    34	
    35	A certified collection professional should be able to:
    36	
    37	- View collection work for which they are qualified.
    38	- Accept or decline an offered collection assignment.
    39	- Record that a sample was collected and sealed.
    40	- Record their current location.
    41	- Hand off and confirm the transfer of the sealed sample to a relay courier or facility.
    42	
    43	### Relay courier
    44	
    45	A relay courier should be able to:
    46	
    47	- View delivery work assigned to them.
    48	- Accept or decline an offered transport assignment.
    49	- See only the details needed for their assigned leg.
    50	- Record location and progress updates.
    51	- Confirm pickup and handoff with the other party.
    52	
    53	### Node handler
    54	
    55	A node handler should be able to:
    56	
    57	- Accept or decline an offered node assignment.
    58	- Manage samples arriving at and leaving a collection centre or hub.
    59	- Register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system.
    60	- Confirm incoming and outgoing handoffs.
    61	- View and configure regular and cooled capacity at the node they are assigned to.
    62	
    63	### Laboratory intake operator
    64	
    65	A laboratory intake operator should be able to:
    66	
    67	- Accept or decline an offered laboratory assignment.
    68	- View expected samples and configure regular and cooled capacity at the laboratory they are assigned to.
    69	- Confirm that a sample was received.
    70	- Record an exception when a sample cannot be accepted normally.
    71	
    72	### Dispatcher
    73	
    74	A dispatcher should be able to:
    75	
    76	- Monitor samples, workers, collection nodes, laboratories, routes and exceptions.
    77	- See the current holder of each sample and whether its latest location is stale.
    78	- View the full journey, including collection and individual transport legs.
    79	- Change, split, merge, cancel or reroute unfinished work.
    80	- Replan unfinished work when a worker, node, route, laboratory or capacity pool becomes unavailable.
    81	- Search the complete audit history of a request or sample.
    82	
    83	Completed work and confirmed custody must not be rewritten during replanning.
    84	
    85	### Administrator
    86	
    87	An administrator may also do everything a dispatcher can do.
    88	
    89	In addition, only an administrator can:
    90	
    91	- Manage users, roles and professional certifications, including which node or laboratory a node handler or laboratory intake operator is assigned to.
    92	- Create and update collection nodes and laboratories.
    93	- Create and update sample types and their handling attributes.
    94	- Activate or deactivate a location, an individual function it provides, or a connection, without restarting the application.
    95	- Configure service coverage, travel times, handling times and laboratory capabilities.
    96	- Configure regular and cooled capacity for any node, laboratory, or transport connection.
    97	
    98	## Collection requests
    99	
   100	A collection request records where and when a sample can be collected and when it must reach the laboratory:
   101	
   102	- **Origin** — a patient’s home, a clinic, or a network node.
   103	- **Sample type** — see Sample types below.
   104	- **Collection window** — the earliest and latest time at which the sample may be collected. Collection must take place inside this window.
   105	- **Delivery deadline** — the time by which the sample must be received at the laboratory.
   106	
   107	The collection window and the delivery deadline are separate constraints: the window governs when pickup may happen, the deadline governs when laboratory receipt must happen. A plan is valid only when collection takes place within the collection window and the sample can still reach an accepting laboratory before its delivery deadline.
   108	
   109	## Pre-sealed samples
   110	
   111	A certified collection professional, relay courier, node handler, or laboratory intake operator may register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system — the person registering it must be the one who currently holds it.
   112	
   113	- Its origin must be a clinic or a network node — not a home.
   114	- The system should create only the transport legs needed from the point of registration onward.
   115	
   116	## Sample types
   117	
   118	Every sample has a type that determines its handling rules, and those rules apply for the whole journey, from collection through laboratory receipt. The system must have at least the following named types available by default: Amber, Indigo, Frost, Pulse. Each of the four requires a qualified collector — only a certified collection professional holding the matching qualification may collect it.
   119	
   120	- **Amber** — standard handling.
   121	- **Indigo** — must not share a container with an Amber sample.
   122	- **Frost** — requires cooled storage and transport throughout its entire journey.
   123	- **Pulse** — time-critical; it must not wait to be combined into a consolidation batch and must be routed without batching delay.
   124	
   125	These named rules are in addition to the generic handling attributes (container, temperature range, qualified-collector requirement, and incompatibilities).
   126	
   127	## Network locations
   128	
   129	The transport network is made up of locations. A single location — a node — may act as a collection point, a transfer point, a hub, a laboratory, or any combination of these (for example, a hub that also acts as a laboratory).
   130	
   131	- **Collection point** — where samples are collected from or enter the network. Serviceability is measured from active collection points.
   132	- **Transfer point / hub** — where a sample changes custody or moves between transport legs.
   133	- **Laboratory** — where a sample is received and its journey completes; a laboratory accepts specific sample types.
   134	
   135	A location may perform several of these functions at the same time.
   136	
   137	## Journey and assignment rules
   138	
   139	The system must support direct, multi-stop and batched journeys.
   140	
   141	A journey may contain several separately assigned transport legs. For example:
   142	
   143	1. Patient’s home to a local collection centre
   144	2. Local collection centre to a hub
   145	3. Hub to the laboratory
   146	
   147	Each movement between two locations is a separate assignment and may be handled by a different worker.
   148	
   149	Collection must happen before transport. Pickup must happen before delivery, and responsibility for the sample must be transferred through a confirmed handoff before the next person continues the journey.

     5	Home samples must be collected and sealed by a certified collection professional before they can enter the transport network. Once sealed, a sample may pass through relay couriers, collection centres and hubs before reaching the laboratory.

     7	Dispatchers currently coordinate much of this work through calls, chat groups, and spreadsheets. This makes it difficult to track custody, use available capacity, assign work fairly, combine compatible samples, and recover when part of the network becomes unavailable.

    11	## Users and responsibilities

    13	Use role-based access control for both actions and data: each user may perform actions and see data only as permitted by the role or roles they currently hold.

    23	
    24	A requester should be able to:

    27	- Create a home or clinic collection request.

    29	- See only requests that belong to them.
    30	
    31	The serviceability check must be a dry run. It must not create a request, sample, journey, assignment or capacity reservation.

    34

    36	
    37	- View collection work for which they are qualified.
    38	- Accept or decline an offered collection assignment.
    39	- Record that a sample was collected and sealed.
    40	- Record their current location.
    41	- Hand off and confirm the transfer of the sealed sample to a relay courier or facility.
    42	
    43	### Relay courier
    44	
    45	A relay courier should be able to:
    46	
    47	- View delivery work assigned to them.
    48	- Accept or decline an offered transport assignment.
    49	- See only the details needed for their assigned leg.
    50	- Record location and progress updates.
    51	- Confirm pickup and handoff with the other party.
    52	
    53	### Node handler
    54	
    55	A node handler should be able to:
    56	
    57	- Accept or decline an offered node assignment.
    58	- Manage samples arriving at and leaving a collection centre or hub.
    59	- Register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system.
    60	- Confirm incoming and outgoing handoffs.
    61	- View and configure regular and cooled capacity at the node they are assigned to.
    62	
    63	### Laboratory intake operator
    64	
    65	A laboratory intake operator should be able to:
    66	
    67	- Accept or decline an offered laboratory assignment.
    68	- View expected samples and configure regular and cooled capacity at the laboratory they are assigned to.
    69	- Confirm that a sample was received.
    70	- Record an exception when a sample cannot be accepted normally.
    71	
    72	### Dispatcher
    73	
    74	A dispatcher should be able to:
    75	
    76	- Monitor samples, workers, collection nodes, laboratories, routes and exceptions.
    77	- See the current holder of each sample and whether its latest location is stale.
    78	- View the full journey, including collection and individual transport legs.
    79	- Change, split, merge, cancel or reroute unfinished work.
    80	- Replan unfinished work when a worker, node, route, laboratory or capacity pool becomes unavailable.
    81	- Search the complete audit history of a request or sample.
    82	
    83	Completed work and confirmed custody must not be rewritten during replanning.
    84	
    85	### Administrator
    86	
    87	An administrator may also do everything a dispatcher can do.
    88	
    89	In addition, only an administrator can:
    90	
    91	- Manage users, roles and professional certifications, including which node or laboratory a node handler or laboratory intake operator is assigned to.
    92	- Create and update collection nodes and laboratories.
    93	- Create and update sample types and their handling attributes.
    94	- Activate or deactivate a location, an individual function it provides, or a connection, without restarting the application.
    95	- Configure service coverage, travel times, handling times and laboratory capabilities.
    96	- Configure regular and cooled capacity for any node, laboratory, or transport connection.
    97	
    98	## Collection requests
    99	
   100	A collection request records where and when a sample can be collected and when it must reach the laboratory:
   101	
   102	- **Origin** — a patient’s home, a clinic, or a network node.
   103	- **Sample type** — see Sample types below.
   104	- **Collection window** — the earliest and latest time at which the sample may be collected. Collection must take place inside this window.
   105	- **Delivery deadline** — the time by which the sample must be received at the laboratory.
   106	
   107	The collection window and the delivery deadline are separate constraints: the window governs when pickup may happen, the deadline governs when laboratory receipt must happen. A plan is valid only when collection takes place within the collection window and the sample can still reach an accepting laboratory before its delivery deadline.
   108	
   109	## Pre-sealed samples
   110	
   111	A certified collection professional, relay courier, node handler, or laboratory intake operator may register a sample that was already collected and sealed before entering the system — the person registering it must be the one who currently holds it.
   112	
   113	- Its origin must be a clinic or a network node — not a home.
   114	- The system should create only the transport legs needed from the point of registration onward.
   115	
   116	## Sample types
   117	
   118	Every sample has a type that determines its handling rules, and those rules apply for the whole journey, from collection through laboratory receipt. The system must have at least the following named types available by default: Amber, Indigo, Frost, Pulse. Each of the four requires a qualified collector — only a certified collection professional holding the matching qualification may collect it.
   119	
   120	- **Amber** — standard handling.
   121	- **Indigo** — must not share a container with an Amber sample.
   122	- **Frost** — requires cooled storage and transport throughout its entire journey.
   123	- **Pulse** — time-critical; it must not wait to be combined into a consolidation batch and must be routed without batching delay.
